Thirdly, because in this life they are tried by various tribulations, temptations and adversities. Yet she owns herself beautiful, because there are always many virtuous and holy men in her, and all who are truly made members of her are adorned with charity, infused virtues and the gifts of the Holy Ghost. She has the sacraments too, by which she is daily renewed and made beautiful. So: [[1:4|I am black but beautiful, O ye daughters of Jerusalem|Nigra sum, sed formosa, o filiæ Jerusalem]], that is, souls, or young maidens and particular Churches, [[1:4|as the tents of Cedar|sicut tabernacula Cedar]]: Cedar was the second son of Ismael[[Gen 25:13||]], and lived with his offspring and household in tents, in the wilderness or desert; and so his tents, though at times unsightly without, being exposed to winds and rains, were within full of riches and cattle. [[1:4|as the curtains of Solomon|sicut pelles Salomonis]] [Latin *pelles*, skins or hides, where the Douay-Rheims has "curtains"]: with which he adorned his house or bridal chamber, or covered the tabernacle of God or its vessels. But Solomon is better understood as Christ, whose skins are the fair garments of his ministers and the ornaments of divine worship, and also the manners and outward bearing, the gait and attire of Christ himself, to which his Bride conforms herself as far as she can. For with these, as with the finest skins, the Church is clothed and adorned. Lastly, by the tents of Cedar may be understood the faithless and the heathen, to whom unbelieving Judea, despising the Church, reckoned her alike.

paras.t: Nolite me considerare, quod fusca sim, id est obscura seu denigrata, juxta sensum quo dixi, Nigra sum; quia decoloravit me sol, id est, comparatione sanctitatis, perfectionis ac sapientiæ sponsi mei, qui est Sol sapientiæ atque justitiæ, fuscam me fateor: qui etiam legem tantæ perfectionis contulit mihi, quod a perfecta ejus observatione deficio; sicque legis suæ splendore me fuscam demonstrat. Rursus, Decoloravit me sol, id est, intuitu et amore solis istius, videlicet sponsi, exposui me tribulationibus, persecutionibus ac aspernationibus impiorum, laboribusque diversis ac multis doloribus: propter quos videor decolorata, et quasi relicta a sponso. Sed hæc omnia intus me ornant: idcirco nolite ista in me ita considerare, ut metu sustinendi talia, recedatis a fide et obedientia mea; sed præmia illa æterna pro his momentaneis afflictionibus exhibenda, perpendite, et gaudete in talibus, sicut in Evangelio sponsus hortatur: Gaudete in illa hora et exsultate, quoniam merces vestra copiosa est in cœlis. Postremo, per solem hoc loco quidam æstum tribulationis intelligunt.
paras.en: [[1:5|Do not consider me that I am brown|Nolite me considerare, quod fusca sim]], that is, dark or blackened, in the sense in which I said, [[1:4|I am black|Nigra sum]]; [[1:5|because the sun hath altered my colour|quia decoloravit me sol]]: that is, I confess myself brown in comparison with the holiness, perfection and wisdom of my Bridegroom, who is the Sun of wisdom and justice; who has also given me a law of such perfection that I fall short of keeping it perfectly; and so by the splendour of his law he shows me to be brown. Again, [[1:5|the sun hath altered my colour|decoloravit me sol]]: that is, for the sake of beholding and loving this Sun, namely the Bridegroom, I have exposed myself to tribulations, persecutions and the contempt of the wicked, to labours of many kinds and many sorrows; because of which I seem discoloured, and as it were forsaken by the Bridegroom. But all these adorn me within; therefore do not so consider these things in me that for fear of suffering the like you draw back from my faith and obedience; but weigh those eternal rewards that are to be given for these momentary afflictions, and rejoice in such things, as the Bridegroom exhorts in the Gospel: [[Matt 5:12|Be glad|Gaudete]] in that hour [[Matt 5:12|and rejoice for your reward is very great in heaven|et exsultate, quoniam merces vestra copiosa est in cœlis]] [Denis's "in that hour" is closer to Luke 6:23, "in that day"]. Lastly, some take the sun in this place for the heat of tribulation.

paras.t: Filii matris meæ pugnaverunt contra me. Ecclesia primitiva ex Judæis atque gentilibus fuit collecta, sicque mater Ecclesiæ partim fuit ipsa gentilitas, partim plebs Judæorum. Ipsam autem Ecclesiam primitivam multis annis acerrime impugnaverunt tam infideles ac obstinati Judæi, quam gentiles increduli, prout in Actibus Apostolorum partim describitur, atque in chronicis, historiis et legendis Sanctorum plenius continetur. Judæi autem impugnaverunt eam tam allegationibus Scripturarum veteris Testamenti, quam persecutione reali. Similiter gentiles philosophi, ratione naturali variis modis contra Ecclesiam dimicarunt; reges vero et tyranni fecerunt hoc gladio materiali. Et sicut sponsus prædixit, tradebantur credentes in eum a parentibus, fratribus, cognatis et amicis, et morte afficiebantur ab eis. — Insuper universalis Ecclesia in persona particularium Ecclesiarum, hoc est quæcumque particularis Ecclesia, dicere potest: Filii matris meæ, hoc est hæretici qui ad tempus fuerunt universalis Ecclesiæ filii (de quibus in prima sua Canonica ait Joannes apostolus, Ex nobis exierunt, sed non erant ex nobis), pugnaverunt contra me, quia valde fuerunt infesti Catholicis, potissime Ariani: qui et corporaliter pluribus annis persequebantur et jugulabant fideles. Similiter impii Christiani, schismatici, principesque iniqui et vitiosi prælati pugnant adversus Ecclesiam, justos vexando, pusillos ac subditos scandalizando, injusta prælia suscitando, aut ecclesiasticis non obediendo mandatis. Et certe pia mater Ecclesia, quæ a malignis spiritibus et ab infidelibus populis incessanter gravissime impugnatur, non mediocriter contristatur, dum filios suos, qui se deberent mutuo contra prætactos hostes acerrimos adjuvare, videt contra se matrem ipsorum et contra se invicem decertare.
paras.en: [[1:5|the sons of my mother have fought against me|Filii matris meæ pugnaverunt contra me]]. The early Church was gathered from Jews and Gentiles, and so the mother of the Church was partly the Gentile world itself and partly the Jewish people. And this early Church was most fiercely assailed for many years both by the unbelieving and obstinate Jews and by the unbelieving Gentiles, as is described in part in the Acts of the Apostles and is set out more fully in the chronicles, histories and legends of the Saints. The Jews assailed her both by citing the Scriptures of the Old Testament and by actual persecution. So too the Gentile philosophers fought against the Church in various ways by natural reason; while kings and tyrants did so with the material sword. And as the Bridegroom foretold, those who believed in him were betrayed by parents, brethren, kinsmen and friends, and were put to death by them [see Luke 21:16]. Moreover, the universal Church in the person of the particular Churches, that is, any particular Church, can say: [[1:5|the sons of my mother|Filii matris meæ]], that is, the heretics who for a time were sons of the universal Church (of whom the apostle John says in his first canonical Epistle: [[1 John 2:19|They went out from us but they were not of us|Ex nobis exierunt, sed non erant ex nobis]]), [[1:5|have fought against me|pugnaverunt contra me]], because they were very hostile to Catholics, above all the Arians, who also for many years persecuted and slaughtered the faithful in body. So too wicked Christians, schismatics, unjust princes and vicious prelates fight against the Church, by harassing the just, by scandalizing the little ones and their subjects, by stirring up unjust wars, or by not obeying the commands of the Church. And truly our loving mother the Church, who is ceaselessly and most grievously assailed by evil spirits and by unbelieving peoples, is not a little saddened when she sees her sons, who ought to help one another against those fiercest enemies just named, fighting against their own mother and against one another.

paras.t: Posuerunt me custodem in vineis : id est, infideles Judæi me in terra sua persequendo, atque ex ea me repellendo, fuerunt occasio, quod cœpi per totam gentilitatem dispergi, atque gentilibus toto orbe terrarum evangelizare: in quibus innumerabilia millia paganorum converti, et multas fundavi particulares Ecclesias, tanquam vineas Dei, quas pastorali sollicitudine custodivi, excolui, fecundavi. Hinc in apostolicis Actis Paulus et Barnabas obduratis loquuntur Judæis: Vobis oportebat primum loqui verbum Dei; sed quia repulistis illud, et indignos vos judicastis vitæ æternæ, ecce convertimur ad gentes: sic enim præcepit nobis Dominus, Posui te in lucem gentibus, ut sis salus mea usque ad ultimum terræ. Vineam meam non custodivi : id est, Synagogam mihi commissam juste reliqui : et hoc, propter obstinationem, rebellionem, et incorrigibilitatem ipsius. Primitivæ namque Ecclesiæ, id est Apostolis et eorum adjutoribus, jussit Christus primo prædicare Judæis. Nam ante passionem suam præcepit : In viam gentium ne abieritis; sed potius ite ad oves, quæ perierunt, domus Israel. Post resurrectionem vero præcepit eisdem Apostolis : Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ. Nihilo minus intentio Christi fuit, ut adhuc primo ad tempus prædicarent Judæis : quod et pene per tredecim annos fecerunt pro majori parte ipsi gloriosi Apostoli, quousque divisi sunt. Interim tamen a tempore persecutionis factæ sub Stephano, sub qua (præter Apostolos) omnes discipuli fuerunt dispersi, coeperunt per totam Galilæam atque Samariam prædicare, sicut et Paulus ac Barnabas alibi : attamen Judæis dumtaxat, sicut in Actibus Apostolorum manifeste habetur. Tandem Judæis undique obduratis, ad gentilium conversionem profecti sunt.
paras.en: [[1:5|they have made me the keeper in the vineyards|Posuerunt me custodem in vineis]]: that is, the unbelieving Jews, by persecuting me in their land and driving me out of it, were the occasion of my beginning to be scattered through the whole Gentile world and to preach the Gospel to the Gentiles throughout the world; among whom I converted countless thousands of pagans and founded many particular Churches, as vineyards of God, which I kept, tilled and made fruitful with pastoral care. Hence in the Acts of the Apostles Paul and Barnabas say to the hardened Jews: [[Acts 13:46|To you it behoved us first to speak the word of God: but because you reject it and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold we turn to the Gentiles|Vobis oportebat primum loqui verbum Dei; sed quia repulistis illud, et indignos vos judicastis vitæ æternæ, ecce convertimur ad gentes]]: [[Acts 13:47|For so the Lord hath commanded us|sic enim præcepit nobis Dominus]], [[Is 49:6|I have given thee to be the light of the Gentiles, that thou mayst be my salvation even to the farthest part of the earth|Posui te in lucem gentibus, ut sis salus mea usque ad ultimum terræ]] [the margin gives both Acts 13:46–47 and Is. xlix, 6, which the Apostles are quoting; Denis's "my salvation" follows Isaias]. [[1:5|my vineyard I have not kept|Vineam meam non custodivi]]: that is, I justly left the Synagogue entrusted to me, and this because of its obstinacy, rebellion and incorrigibility. For Christ commanded the early Church, that is, the Apostles and their helpers, to preach first to the Jews. For before his passion he commanded: [[Matt 10:5|Go ye not into the way of the Gentiles|In viam gentium ne abieritis]]; [[Matt 10:6|But go ye rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel|sed potius ite ad oves, quæ perierunt, domus Israel]]. But after the resurrection he commanded the same Apostles: [[Mark 16:15|Go ye into the whole world and preach the gospel to every creature|Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ]]. Nevertheless it was Christ's intention that they should still preach first to the Jews for a time; and this the glorious Apostles themselves did for the most part for nearly thirteen years, until they were separated. In the meantime, however, from the time of the persecution raised under Stephen, in which all the disciples except the Apostles were scattered[[Acts 8:1||]], they began to preach through all Galilee and Samaria, as did Paul and Barnabas elsewhere, yet to the Jews only, as is plainly found in the Acts of the Apostles[[Acts 13:46||]]. At last, when the Jews were hardened everywhere, they set out to convert the Gentiles.

paras.t: Insuper Ecclesia ex persona carnalium ac negligentium prælatorum dicere potest : Posuerunt me custodem in vineis: id est, Christus et ejus Apostoli præceperunt mihi, cum omni diligentia præsidere ac providere particularibus Ecclesiis Dei. Sic namque princeps Apostolorum hortatur : Pascite, qui in vobis est, gregem Dei. Et Paulus : Qui præest, in sollicitudine, supple, præsit. Vineam meam, id est vineas mihi commissas, non custodivi : per singulare intelligendo plurale, ut moris est in Scripturis.
paras.en: Moreover, the Church can say in the person of carnal and negligent prelates: [[1:5|they have made me the keeper in the vineyards|Posuerunt me custodem in vineis]]: that is, Christ and his Apostles commanded me to preside over and provide for the particular Churches of God with all diligence. For so the prince of the Apostles exhorts: [[1 Pet 5:2|Feed the flock of God which is among you|Pascite, qui in vobis est, gregem Dei]]. And Paul: [[Rom 12:8|he that ruleth, with carefulness|Qui præest, in sollicitudine]], supply: let him rule. [[1:5|my vineyard|Vineam meam]], that is, the vineyards entrusted to me, [[1:5|I have not kept|non custodivi]]: understanding the plural by the singular, as is the custom in the Scriptures.

paras.t: Circa hæc ait Anselmus : Quemadmodum vineæ quatuor modis læduntur præcipue, sic sanctæ Ecclesiæ totidem adversa, maxime in suis membris teneris, solent nocere. Vineæ etenim obest asperum frigus, et urens ventus, spissaque grando, et nimia pluvia. Sic sanctæ Ecclesiæ in suis membris aliquando nocet frigus seu torpor exemplorum malorum: quoniam sicut frigus seu gelu stringit atque exterminat vineæ florem, sic malum exemplum aufert a tenero corde conceptæ devotionis amorem. Aliquando etiam ei obest ventus diabolicæ suggestionis, adurens renes mentis et corporis. Nocere etiam maxime solet grando pessimæ detractionis et dissensionis, quæ dissipat florem fraternæ dilectionis. Pluvia quoque pravæ doctrinæ, et prosperitatis assiduæ, solet plerumque statum mentis dissolvere, et ad amorem mundi reflectere. Sicut e contrario prodest vineæ suavis aura cum dulci rore, sic prodest Ecclesiæ pax cum salubri sermone. Præterea, sicut vinitores non custodiunt vineas, qui eas non putant, non considerant, non excolunt, nec fructum ex eis colligere conantur; ita prælati qui sibi commissis pravos mores, inordinata colloquia, opera illicita non præcidunt, nec qualiter subditi circa divinorum observantiam præceptorum se habeant, intuentur; nec corripiendo, corrigendo, exhortando, docendo, obsecrando, comminando, et orando pro eis, reformare eos conantur, neque exemplis neque verbis satagunt fructum virtutum et spiritualem assiduumque profectum ex ipsis producere, nequaquam ut tenentur vineas Dei commissas sibi custodiunt. Ideo sanguinem pereuntium Dominus requiret ab eis.
paras.en: On these words Anselm says: As vineyards are harmed chiefly in four ways, so the same number of adversities are wont to harm holy Church, above all in her tender members. For a vineyard is harmed by bitter cold, scorching wind, thick hail and too much rain. So holy Church is sometimes harmed in her members by the cold or numbness of bad examples: for as cold or frost nips and destroys the flower of the vine, so a bad example takes from a tender heart the love of the devotion it had conceived. Sometimes too she is harmed by the wind of the devil's suggestion, scorching the reins of mind and body. The hail of most wicked detraction and dissension is also wont to do the greatest harm, for it scatters the flower of brotherly love. The rain too of false doctrine and of constant prosperity often loosens the state of the mind and turns it back to the love of the world. As, on the contrary, a gentle breeze with sweet dew does good to the vineyard, so peace with wholesome preaching does good to the Church. Further, as vinedressers do not keep their vineyards who do not prune them, do not look to them, do not till them, and do not try to gather fruit from them; so prelates who do not cut away the evil manners, disorderly talk and unlawful works of those entrusted to them, nor look to how their subjects stand in keeping God's commandments, nor try to reform them by rebuking, correcting, exhorting, teaching, beseeching, threatening and praying for them, nor take pains by example or by word to bring forth from them the fruit of virtues and steady spiritual progress, by no means keep the vineyards of God entrusted to them as they are bound to. Therefore the Lord will require the blood of those who perish at their hands[[Ezech 33:6||]][[Ezech 33:8||]].

paras.t: Sed quoniam primitiva Ecclesia a Judæis dispersa, et per gentilitatem divisa, innumerabiles persecutiones sustinuit, sicut et Paulus in suis epistolis de se patefecit, recte subjungit Ecclesia : Indica mihi, quem diligit anima mea, ubi pascas, ubi cubes in meridie : id est, tu, sponse cœlestis super omnia prædilecte, mihi dignanter ostende ubi tu gratiose commoreris, in quorum cordibus pabula internæ refectionis exhibeas, quos pastoraliter nutris. Indica etiam mihi ubi cubes, id est, stabiliter requiescas, quorum mentes tibi carissimas luce contemplationis perfundas : ita quod per contemplativæ exercitia vitæ, te intra se jugiter complectuntur, retinent, nec offendunt, ita ut illud Deuteronomii impleatur in eis : Amantissimus Domini habitabit confidenter; in eo quasi in thalamo tota die morabitur, et inter humeros illius requiescet.
paras.en: But since the early Church, scattered by the Jews and spread through the Gentile world, endured countless persecutions, as Paul too makes known of himself in his epistles[[2 Cor 11:23||]] [the margin gives II Cor. xi, 23–27], the Church rightly adds: [[1:6|Shew me, O thou whom my soul loveth, where thou feedest, where thou liest in the midday|Indica mihi, quem diligit anima mea, ubi pascas, ubi cubes in meridie]]: that is, thou, heavenly Bridegroom, beloved above all things, graciously show me where thou dost dwell in thy grace, in whose hearts thou dost set the food of inward refreshment, whom thou dost feed as a shepherd. [[1:6|Shew me|Indica mihi]] also [[1:6|where thou liest|ubi cubes]], that is, where thou dost steadfastly rest: whose minds, most dear to thee, thou dost flood with the light of contemplation, so that through the exercises of the contemplative life they hold thee constantly embraced within them, keep thee, and do not offend thee; so that that word of Deuteronomy is fulfilled in them: [[Deut 33:12|The best beloved of the Lord shall dwell confidently in him: as in a bride chamber shall he abide all the day long, and between his shoulders shall be rest|Amantissimus Domini habitabit confidenter; in eo quasi in thalamo tota die morabitur, et inter humeros illius requiescet]].

paras.t: Indica (inquam) mihi, ubi sic pascas, sic cubes in meridie, id est in præcipuo gratiæ tuæ splendore, in magno caritatis fervore, in illuminatione præclara : quemadmodum in Regum libris David fatetur : Spiritus Domini locutus est per me, sicut meridiana lux clara est et absque nubibus rutilat. Quamvis autem sponsus inter cives regni cœlestis potissime cubet, qui meridiana ejus cognitione lætantur, atque per beatificam visionem sponso gloriæ inavertibiliter ac tranquillissime sunt intenti; attamen etiam in hac vita in viris contemplativis, perfectis, heroicis, aliqualiter cubat : quibus scripsit Apostolus, Pax Christi exsultet semper in cordibus vestris; quorum unusquisque dicere potest, In pace in id ipsum dormiam et requiescam. Unde et ipse per Isaiam loquitur : Super quem requiescet spiritus meus, nisi super quietum et humilem?
paras.en: [[1:6|Shew me|Indica]] (I say) where thou dost thus feed and thus [[1:6|liest in the midday|cubes in meridie]]: that is, in the chief splendour of thy grace, in the great fervour of charity, in a glorious illumination; as David confesses in the books of Kings: [[2 Kings 23:2|The spirit of the Lord hath spoken by me|Spiritus Domini locutus est per me]], as the midday light is clear and shineth [[2 Kings 23:4|without clouds|absque nubibus]] [Denis's wording; the Vulgate of 2 Kings 23:4 has "as the light of the morning … shineth in the morning without clouds"]. Now although the Bridegroom lies most of all among the citizens of the heavenly kingdom, who rejoice in the midday knowledge of him and through the beatific vision are fixed upon the Bridegroom of glory unswervingly and most tranquilly, yet even in this life he lies in some measure in contemplative, perfect and heroic men: to whom the Apostle wrote, [[Col 3:15|let the peace of Christ rejoice in your hearts|Pax Christi exsultet semper in cordibus vestris]] [Denis adds "always"]; and each of whom can say: [[Ps 4:9|In peace in the self same I will sleep, and I will rest|In pace in id ipsum dormiam et requiescam]]. Hence he himself also says through Isaias: Upon whom shall my spirit rest, but upon him that is quiet and humble?[[Is 66:2||]] [this is the older Latin reading of Is 66:2, made from the Greek; the Vulgate and the Douay-Rheims have: to whom shall I have respect, but to him that is poor and little]

paras.t: Hæc itaque petit sibi indicari Ecclesia, quatenus ex eorum consideratione consoletur et glorietur in Domino inter tot adversitatum suarum pressuras, et ut videat ipsa pia mater, in quibus prædicatio sua fructificet. Ideo quoque postulat sibi ista monstrari, quoniam scit se sua exteriori prædicatione in audientibus nil posse proficere, nisi sponsus in illorum cordibus intus loquatur, suaque unctione dociles et attentos faciat eos : ob hoc appetit invenire ac scire hujusmodi auditores. Unde subjungit : ne vagari incipiam, id est, ne infructuose discurram, post greges sodalium tuorum, id est ad conventicula reproborum, post multitudines obstinatorum atque hæreticorum : qui post unam et secundam correptionem vitandi sunt. Unde in Ecclesiastico scriptum est : Ubi non est auditus, non effundas sermonem. Et Salomon : In auribus insipientium ne loquaris, quia despicient doctrinam eloquii tui; Qui erudit derisorem, ipse sibi injuriam facit. Nam et sponsus in Evangelio jussit : Nolite sanctum dare canibus, neque margaritas vestras projiciatis ante porcos. Verum quamdiu ignorat Ecclesia, quis docilis indocilisve exsistat, debet omnibus prædicare, sicut in simili loquitur Augustinus : Nescientes quis ad electorum aut reproborum societatem pertineat, debemus beneficium fraternæ correptionis impendere cunctis.
paras.en: These things, then, the Church asks to be shown her, so that by considering them she may be consoled and may glory in the Lord amid the pressures of so many adversities, and so that this loving mother may see in whom her preaching bears fruit. She asks to be shown them also because she knows that by her outward preaching she can profit her hearers nothing, unless the Bridegroom speaks inwardly in their hearts and by his anointing makes them teachable and attentive: for this reason she longs to find and to know hearers of this kind. Hence she adds: [[1:6|lest I begin to wander|ne vagari incipiam]], that is, lest I run about to no purpose, [[1:6|after the flocks of thy companions|post greges sodalium tuorum]], that is, to the gatherings of the reprobate, after the multitudes of the obstinate and of heretics, who are to be avoided [[Tit 3:10|after the first and second admonition|post unam et secundam correptionem]]. Hence it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 32:6|Where there is no hearing, pour not out words|Ubi non est auditus, non effundas sermonem]]. And Solomon: [[Prov 23:9|Speak not in the ears of fools: because they will despise the instruction of thy speech|In auribus insipientium ne loquaris, quia despicient doctrinam eloquii tui]]; [[Prov 9:7|He that teacheth a scorner, doth an injury to himself|Qui erudit derisorem, ipse sibi injuriam facit]]. For the Bridegroom too commanded in the Gospel: [[Matt 7:6|Give not that which is holy to dogs; neither cast ye your pearls before swine|Nolite sanctum dare canibus, neque margaritas vestras projiciatis ante porcos]]. But so long as the Church does not know who is teachable and who unteachable, she ought to preach to all, as Augustine says in a like case: Not knowing who belongs to the company of the elect and who to that of the reprobate, we ought to bestow the benefit of fraternal correction upon all.

paras.t: At vero per sodales, quidam intelligunt hæresiarchas et seductores ac impios præsidentes, qui sibi subjectos damnationi secum involvunt : et sodales sponsi vocantur, vel quia se nominant ejus vicarios, et vocant se Christianos; vel quia in potestate seu prælatione cum eo communicant, aut quia in natura humanitatis cum eo conveniunt. Alii, per sodales intelligunt angelos sanctos, qui singulis gentibus et communitatibus præsunt, quemadmodum in Ecclesiastico legitur : Rectorem in unaquaque præposuit gente. Unde et in Daniele de principe Græcorum et principe Persarum aliqua continentur. Per quos (sicut divinus docet Dionysius) angeli sancti de choro Principatuum designantur : qui sunt sodales Christi per gloriæ communionem et prælationis participationem.
paras.en: But by the companions some understand heresiarchs, seducers and impious rulers, who drag those subject to them into damnation along with themselves; and they are called the Bridegroom's companions either because they name themselves his vicars and call themselves Christians, or because they share with him in power or prelacy, or because they are one with him in the nature of manhood. Others understand by the companions the holy angels, who are set over the several nations and communities, as we read in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 17:14|Over every nation he set a ruler|Rectorem in unaquaque præposuit gente]]. Hence in Daniel too some things are told of the prince of the Greeks and the prince of the Persians. By these (as the divine Dionysius teaches) are signified holy angels of the choir of Principalities, who are Christ's companions by the communion of glory and a share in rule.

paras.t: Amplius sic potest exponi, quod sponsa precatur sibi a sponso indicari ubi in meridie cubet, ita quod, quamvis sciat per fidem sponsum in mentibus Beatorum cubare, nihilo minus petit sibi hoc clariori illuminatione monstrari : quatenus sinceriter contemplando gloriam Beatorum, et quam dignantissime, intime atque dulcissime sponsus requiescat in eis, consolationem accipiat, et ad laborandum infatigabiliter animetur, nec deviet sequendo errantes.
paras.en: Further, it can be explained thus: the bride prays that the Bridegroom show her where he lies in the midday, in such a way that, although she knows by faith that the Bridegroom lies in the minds of the Blessed, she nonetheless asks that this be shown her by a clearer illumination; so that, by contemplating more purely the glory of the Blessed, and how most graciously, inwardly and sweetly the Bridegroom rests in them, she may receive consolation and be roused to labour untiringly, and not go astray by following those who err.

paras.t: Postremo per appropriationem dicere possumus, quod sponsus in activis hominibus pascit, in contemplativis cubat. Activi namque non sunt tam diu tamque frequenter intenti actualiter sponso, ut contemplativi; sed certis horis pascit eos, pasciturque ab eis in membris suis vel in se ipso, dum de eorum bonis gaudet operibus, atque eorum congratulatur profectui. Unde in Apocalypsi testatur : Ego sto ad ostium et pulso : si quis aperuerit mihi, intrabo ad illum, et cœnabo cum eo, et ipse mecum. In contemplativis autem cubat, id est quiescit, quoniam contemplativi stabilius frequentiusque vacant sponsi amplexibus, et pulchritudinem vultus ejus prospiciunt.
paras.en: Lastly, by appropriation [that is, assigning to each what belongs to it more particularly] we may say that the Bridegroom feeds among men of the active life and lies among contemplatives. For active men are not so long or so often actually intent upon the Bridegroom as contemplatives are; but at certain hours he feeds them, and is fed by them, in his members or in himself, when he rejoices in their good works and is glad at their progress. Hence he testifies in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 3:20|I stand at the gate and knock|Ego sto ad ostium et pulso]]: if any man open to me, [[Apoc 3:20|I will come in to him and will sup with him: and he with me|intrabo ad illum, et cœnabo cum eo, et ipse mecum]]. But among contemplatives he lies, that is, rests, since contemplatives give themselves more steadily and more often to the Bridegroom's embraces, and gaze upon the beauty of his face.

paras.t: Sequitur sponsi responsio ad præinductam sponsæ petitionem. Si ignoras te, o pulchra inter mulieres, id est, quia ignorare te ipsam non debes, nec in toto te nescis, o Ecclesia, præ ceteris gentibus gratia ac virtutibus speciosa. Sæpissime equidem in Scripturis accipitur si, pro non, ut quum sanctus Job loquitur : Si deceptum est cor meum super muliere, et si ad ostium amici mei insidiatus sum. Certum est autem, quod Ecclesia quæ teste sponso censetur pulchra, non ignoret se ipsam : imo scit quid per naturam exsistat, quod a sponso redempta sit, et Baptismate renovata, variisque gratiarum charismatibus redempta. Itaque, quoniam non ignoras te, egredere, id est, in actum virtutum et in officium prædicationis procede ; et pasce hædos tuos, id est, non solum justos et simplices, qui oves vocantur, sed etiam peccatores et impios instrue, nutri, guberna, juxta tabernacula pastorum, id est ad imitationem præcedentium patrum, et juxta documenta Apostolorum, qui indifferenter universis prædicaverunt : sicque et abi post vestigia gregum tuorum, id est, virtutes et opera electarum congregationum sectare, ne inutiliter evageris. Optimum enim est et valde securum, tritam Sanctorum incedere viam, et eorum inhærere vestigiis, qui cursum suum feliciter compleverunt. Noli ergo immoderate discutere aut velle cognoscere, in quibus ego per gratiam habitem, aut qui electi sint et digni ut eis prædicatio fiat : imo quo aliqui magis corrupti sunt, eo plus stude eis succurrere : quia etsi contigerit eos perire, tu tamen fructu tuorum non carebis laborum. Juxta præhabitum sensum ait Apostolus : An ignoratis vos ipsos? nisi forte reprobi sitis. Et denuo fassus est : Omnibus debitor sum, sapientibus et insipientibus. Verumtamen multi hunc passum aliter ac prolixe exponunt ; sed explanatio ista facilior aptiorque videtur.
paras.en: There follows the Bridegroom's answer to the bride's petition set out above. [[1:7|If thou know not thyself, O fairest among women|Si ignoras te, o pulchra inter mulieres]] [Denis reads *pulchra*, "fair", for the Vulgate's *pulcherrima*, "fairest"]: that is, since thou oughtest not to be ignorant of thyself, nor art thou wholly unaware of thyself, O Church, beautiful in grace and virtues above the other nations. For very often in the Scriptures *if* is taken for *not*, as when holy Job says: [[Job 31:9|If my heart hath been deceived upon a woman, and if I have laid wait at my friend's door|Si deceptum est cor meum super muliere, et si ad ostium amici mei insidiatus sum]] [that is, my heart has not been deceived, and I have not laid wait]. Now it is certain that the Church, who by the Bridegroom's witness is judged fair, is not ignorant of herself: rather, she knows what she is by nature, and that she has been redeemed by the Bridegroom, renewed by Baptism, and redeemed [the Latin repeats *redempta*, probably a slip for a word such as "adorned"] with the various gifts of graces. So, since thou art not ignorant of thyself, [[1:7|go forth|egredere]], that is, go out into the practice of the virtues and into the office of preaching; [[1:7|and feed thy kids|et pasce hædos tuos]], that is, instruct, nourish and govern not only the just and simple, who are called sheep, but also sinners and the impious, [[1:7|beside the tents of the shepherds|juxta tabernacula pastorum]], that is, in imitation of the fathers who went before, and according to the teachings of the Apostles, who preached to all without distinction; and so [[1:7|follow after the steps of the flocks|abi post vestigia gregum]] (of thy flocks), that is, follow the virtues and works of the chosen congregations, lest thou wander off to no purpose. For it is best and very safe to walk the beaten way of the Saints and to keep close to the footsteps of those who have happily finished their course. Do not therefore inquire immoderately, or wish to know, in whom I dwell by grace, or who are elect and worthy to be preached to: rather, the more corrupt some are, the more strive to help them; for even if it should happen that they perish, thou shalt not lose the fruit of thy labours. In keeping with the sense given above, the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 13:5|Know you not your own selves|An ignoratis vos ipsos]]? [[2 Cor 13:5|unless perhaps you be reprobates|nisi forte reprobi sitis]]. And again he confessed: I am a debtor to all, [[Rom 1:14|to the wise and to the unwise|sapientibus et insipientibus]]. Many, however, explain this passage otherwise and at length; but this explanation seems easier and more fitting.

paras.t: Equitatui meo in curribus Pharaonis assimilavi te, amica mea : id est, o sponsa carissima, ego conformavi et similem feci te exercitui filiorum Israel in dejectione et submersione curruum ac equitum regis Ægypti : quem cum suis in mari Rubro submersi, et exercitum Israel per medium maris illius eduxi ac liberavi. Sic te de potestate diaboli angelorumque ejus redemi. Et sicut filios Israel pavi manna ac aqua de petra educta ; sic te pane cœlesti, corpore et sanguine meo, enutrivi, aqua sapientiæ poto. Et sicut illos per solitudinem ad terram promissionis sub velamento nubis in die, et in splendore ignis in nocte deduxi ; sic te per desertum sæculi hujus exilii, ad cœlestem dirigo paradisum, sub protectione auxilii ac rore refrigerii mei, et in luce fidei ac claritate illustrationis supernæ ac caritatis fervore inter prospera et adversa. Quemadmodum etiam filiis Israel in monte Sinai per Moysen legem dedi ; sic tibi in monte terræ promissionis per me ipsum Evangelicam contuli legem. Hinc in Isaia asseritur : Super omnem gloriam protectio ; et tabernaculum erit in umbraculum diei ab æstu, et in securitatem, et in absconsionem a turbine et a pluvia.
paras.en: [[1:8|To my company of horsemen, in Pharao's chariots, have I likened thee, O my love|Equitatui meo in curribus Pharaonis assimilavi te, amica mea]]: that is, O dearest bride, I have conformed thee and made thee like the army of the children of Israel in the overthrow and drowning of the chariots and horsemen of the king of Egypt, whom with his men I drowned in the Red Sea[[Ex 14:28||]], while I led the army of Israel out through the midst of that sea[[Ex 14:29||]] and set it free[[Ex 14:30||]]. So have I redeemed thee from the power of the devil and his angels. And as I fed the children of Israel with manna[[Ex 16:1||]] and with water brought out of the rock[[Ex 17:6||]][[Num 20:11||]], so have I nourished thee with the bread of heaven, my body and blood, and given thee to drink of the water of wisdom. And as I led them through the wilderness to the land of promise under the covering of the cloud by day and in the brightness of fire by night, so I direct thee through the desert of this world of exile to the heavenly paradise, under the protection of my help and the dew of my refreshment, and in the light of faith, the brightness of heavenly illumination and the fervour of charity, amid prosperity and adversity. And as I gave the law to the children of Israel on Mount Sinai through Moses[[Ex 19:20||]], so on a mountain of the land of promise I have given thee the law of the Gospel through myself. Hence it is declared in Isaias: [[Is 4:5|over all the glory shall be a protection|Super omnem gloriam protectio]]; and [[Is 4:6|there shall be a tabernacle for a shade in the daytime from the heat, and for a security and covert from the whirlwind, and from rain|et tabernaculum erit in umbraculum diei ab æstu, et in securitatem, et in absconsionem a turbine et a pluvia]].

paras.t: Insuper, per æquitatem Dei, possunt intelligi angelicæ potestates et angeli sancti : qui in Scripturis ubertim appellantur exercitus et castra atque militia Dei, juxta illud Psalmi : Currus Dei decem millibus multiplex. In Genesi quoque narratur : Jacob abiit via qua cœperat, fueruntque ei obviam angeli Dei. Quos quum vidisset, dixit : Castra Dei sunt hæc. Unde et alibi legitur : Multa sunt nimis castra Dei fortia, et facientia verbum ejus. Porro per equitatum Pharaonis, bene accipiuntur adversariæ potestates, et angeli tenebrarum, ac acies vitiorum. Potest itaque et sic exponi : O amica, id est, universalis Ecclesia, assimilavi te equitatui meo, id est angelis sanctis, in curribus Pharaonis, id est per hoc, quod præstiti tibi virtutem resistendi ac prævalendi malignis illis spiritibus, quibus et angeli sancti restiterunt ac prævaluerunt in exordio sæculorum, non acquiescendo elationi illorum, sed potius expellendo ipsos de statione cœlesti : juxta illud (secundum unam expositionem) in Apocalypsi : Factum est prælium in cœlo. Michael et angeli ejus præliabantur cum dracone, et draco pugnabat et angeli ejus; et non prævaluerunt, neque inventus est locus eorum amplius in cœlo. Hinc in Evangelio sponsus promittit Ecclesiæ : Ecce dedi vobis potestatem calcandi super serpentes et scorpiones et supra omnem virtutem inimici. Cui et in Psalmo promittitur : Cadent a latere tuo mille, et decem millia a dextris tuis; itemque, Super aspidem et basiliscum ambulabis, et conculcabis leonem et draconem. Ideo Paulus disseruit : Deus conteret Satanam sub pedibus vestris velociter.
paras.en: Moreover, by God's company of horsemen [the Latin has *æquitatem*, "equity", evidently for *equitatum*, "company of horsemen"] may be understood the angelic powers and the holy angels, who in the Scriptures are often called the army, the camps and the host of God, according to that of the Psalm: [[Ps 67:18|The chariot of God is attended by ten thousands|Currus Dei decem millibus multiplex]]. In Genesis too it is related: [[Gen 32:1|Jacob also went on the journey he had begun: and the angels of God met him|Jacob abiit via qua cœperat, fueruntque ei obviam angeli Dei]]. [[Gen 32:2|And when he saw them, he said: These are the camps of God|Quos quum vidisset, dixit : Castra Dei sunt hæc]]. Hence it is read elsewhere also: [[Joel 2:11|his armies are exceedingly great, for they are strong, and execute his word|Multa sunt nimis castra Dei fortia, et facientia verbum ejus]] [Denis has "the camps of God" where the Vulgate has "his camps"]. Pharao's company of horsemen, on the other hand, is well taken for the adverse powers, the angels of darkness, and the battle-lines of the vices. So it can also be explained thus: [[1:8|O my love|O amica]], that is, the universal Church, [[1:8|have I likened thee|assimilavi te]] to [[1:8|my company of horsemen|equitatui meo]], that is, to the holy angels, [[1:8|in Pharao's chariots|in curribus Pharaonis]], that is, in this, that I have given thee strength to resist and to prevail over those malign spirits whom the holy angels also resisted and prevailed over at the beginning of the ages, not consenting to their pride but rather driving them out of their station in heaven; according to that (on one interpretation) in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 12:7|there was a great battle in heaven: Michael and his angels fought with the dragon, and the dragon fought, and his angels|Factum est prælium in cœlo. Michael et angeli ejus præliabantur cum dracone, et draco pugnabat et angeli ejus]]; [[Apoc 12:8|And they prevailed not: neither was their place found any more in heaven|et non prævaluerunt, neque inventus est locus eorum amplius in cœlo]]. Hence in the Gospel the Bridegroom promises the Church: [[Luke 10:19|Behold, I have given you power to tread upon serpents and scorpions and upon all the power of the enemy|Ecce dedi vobis potestatem calcandi super serpentes et scorpiones et supra omnem virtutem inimici]]. To her it is promised in the Psalm too: [[Ps 90:7|A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand|Cadent a latere tuo mille, et decem millia a dextris tuis]]; and again: [[Ps 90:13|Thou shalt walk upon the asp and the basilisk: and thou shalt trample under foot the lion and the dragon|Super aspidem et basiliscum ambulabis, et conculcabis leonem et draconem]]. Therefore Paul declared: God [[Rom 16:20|crush Satan under your feet speedily|conteret Satanam sub pedibus vestris velociter]].

paras.t: Pulchræ sunt genæ tuæ sicut turturis. Circa hoc loquitur Origenes : Paulus apostolus ait : Corpus non est unum membrum, sed multa; vos autem estis corpus Christi, et membra de membro. Et iterum : Nemo carnem suam unquam odio habuit; sed fovet et nutrit eam, sicut et Christus Ecclesiam : quia membra sumus corporis ejus. Per hæc igitur edocemur, quomodo sponsa Christi (quæ est Ecclesia) sit corpus Christi et membra. In quibus membris [sicut] sunt aliqui qui dicuntur oculi, pro intelligentiæ sine dubio et scientiæ lumine; et alii aures, pro audiendo verbo doctrinæ; alii manus, pro bonis operibus religiosisque ministeriis: ita sunt aliqui qui et genæ ejus vocantur. Genæ autem [partes] vultus dicuntur, in quibus honestas et verecundia animæ cognoscuntur: per quod sine dubio illi in membris Ecclesiæ declarantur, qui castitatis et pudicitiæ excolunt honestatem. Pro iis ergo ad totum corpus Ecclesiæ dicitur : Quam pulchræ sunt genæ tuæ! quarum pulchritudinem accepit ex osculo sponsi. Ex tunc enim castitas et pudicitia atque virginitas, quæ prius non fuerant, per Ecclesiæ genas miro decore diffusæ sunt : quæ genarum formositas turturi comparatur. Turturum enim fertur esse natura, ut neque masculus præter unam feminam adeat aliam, neque femina amplius quam unum patiatur marem, ita ut compare exstincto, superstiti cum conjuge exstinctus sit concubitus amor. Convenienter igitur similitudo turturis aptatur pulchritudini, id est pudicitiæ ac castitati, genarum Ecclesiæ : quia Ecclesia alterius viri post Christum nescit conjugium, et quoniam abundantia pudicitiæ ac continentiæ viget in ea. Hæc sententialiter Origenes.
paras.en: [[1:9|Thy cheeks are beautiful as the turtledove's|Pulchræ sunt genæ tuæ sicut turturis]]. On this Origen says: The apostle Paul says: [[1 Cor 12:14|the body also is not one member, but many|Corpus non est unum membrum, sed multa]]; [[1 Cor 12:27|you are the body of Christ and members of member|vos autem estis corpus Christi, et membra de membro]]. And again: [[Eph 5:29|no man ever hated his own flesh, but nourisheth and cherisheth it, as also Christ doth the church|Nemo carnem suam unquam odio habuit; sed fovet et nutrit eam, sicut et Christus Ecclesiam]], because [[Eph 5:30|we are members of him|membra sumus corporis ejus]]. By these words, then, we are taught how the bride of Christ (who is the Church) is the body of Christ and its members. Among these members, as there are some who are called eyes, doubtless for the light of understanding and knowledge, and others ears, for hearing the word of doctrine, and others hands, for good works and religious ministries, so there are some who are called her cheeks. Now the cheeks are said to be the parts of the face in which the modesty and shamefastness of the soul are seen; by which doubtless are signified those among the members of the Church who cultivate the comeliness of chastity and purity. For their sake, then, it is said to the whole body of the Church: [[1:9|Thy cheeks are beautiful|Quam pulchræ sunt genæ tuæ]]! a beauty they received from the kiss of the Bridegroom. For from that time chastity, purity and virginity, which before had not been, have been spread with wonderful grace over the cheeks of the Church; and this loveliness of the cheeks is compared to the turtledove. For the nature of turtledoves is said to be such that neither does the male go to any female but one, nor does the female admit more than one male, so that when its mate has died, the love of union dies in the survivor together with its spouse. Fittingly, then, the likeness of the turtledove is applied to the beauty, that is, the modesty and chastity, of the cheeks of the Church: because the Church knows no marriage with another husband after Christ, and because an abundance of modesty and continence flourishes in her. Thus Origen, in substance.

paras.t: Porro Anselmus et alii, per genas sponsæ intelligunt doctores ac prædicatores Ecclesiæ, quoniam genæ dentes intra se continent, et per eos masticant, terunt et in ventrem projiciunt cibum : sic boni prælati ac prædicatores verbo Dei reficiunt audientes, et difficiliora quæque eis quasi masticando et frangendo exponunt. Insuper genæ sponsæ dicuntur pulchræ ut turturis, quoniam ipsa Ecclesia pro suis et filiorum suorum defectibus et peccatis verecundatur, et ea cum pœnitentiali ac sapientiali pudore humiliter confitetur.
paras.en: Anselm and others, again, understand by the bride's cheeks the doctors and preachers of the Church, since the cheeks hold the teeth within them, and by them chew and grind the food and send it down into the belly: so good prelates and preachers refresh their hearers with the word of God, and expound to them all the harder things, as if by chewing and breaking them up. Moreover, the bride's cheeks are said to be beautiful as the turtledove's because the Church herself is ashamed of her own failings and sins and those of her children, and confesses them humbly with a penitent and wise shame.

paras.t: Collum tuum sicut monilia. Per membra corporea in hoc libro, et per aves ac cetera inanimata ac irrationalia, spiritualium ac rationalium rerum proprietates atque officia designantur. Sicque per collum, quo caput jungitur corpori, per quod cibus descendit in alvum, quod etiam levatur in altum, designantur prælati, qui inter Deum et populum mediant, et mysticum corpus Christi (puta Ecclesiam) suo capiti, videlicet Christo, jungunt : cui sibi commissos reconciliare tenentur, orando et sacrificando pro ipsis, eosque corripiendo, purgando, ac fovendo in bonis, gratiarum quoque charismata impetrando eis a Domino. Hi instar colli erigantur in altum ecclesiastica dignitate atque prælatica potestate; et spiritualis alimonia a capite Christo descendens, per ipsos in greges ipsis creditos derivatur. Hoc collum ornatur et assimilatur monilibus. Monilia namque, sunt ornamenta ad claudendum pectus formata, suntque virginum signa desponsatarum. Et dicitur monile, a monendo: quia dum puellæ desponsatæ apponitur, eam hortatur, ne alterum amatorem admittat, sed suo fidem sponso conservet. Quum itaque boni prælati solliciti sint et laborent subditorum suorum pectora adornare, atque a pravis ea cogitationibus claudere, quatenus sponso pura et inviolata exhibeantur, nec adulterinum adspiciant seductorem diabolum, neque ad aliquem sensualiter afficiantur: recte monilibus comparantur ipsi prælati.
paras.en: [[1:9|thy neck as jewels|Collum tuum sicut monilia]]. In this book the properties and offices of spiritual and rational things are signified by the members of the body, and by birds and other inanimate and irrational things. And so by the neck, by which the head is joined to the body, through which food goes down into the belly, and which is also raised on high, are signified the prelates, who mediate between God and the people, and join the mystical body of Christ (that is, the Church) to its head, namely Christ: to whom they are bound to reconcile those committed to them, by praying and offering sacrifice for them, by correcting and cleansing them and cherishing them in good, and by obtaining for them from the Lord the gifts of graces. These are raised on high like a neck by ecclesiastical dignity and prelatial power; and the spiritual nourishment coming down from Christ the head is passed on through them to the flocks entrusted to them. This neck is adorned with jewels and likened to them. For *monilia* [the word rendered "jewels"] are ornaments made to close the breast, and are the tokens of betrothed maidens. And *monile* is so called from *monere* ["to warn"]: because when it is put on a betrothed girl it exhorts her not to admit another lover, but to keep faith with her own bridegroom. Since, then, good prelates are careful and labour to adorn the breasts of their subjects and to close them against evil thoughts, so that they may be presented to the Bridegroom pure and inviolate, and may not look upon the adulterous seducer, the devil, nor be attached to anyone by sensual love, these prelates are rightly compared to jewels.

paras.t: Porro, secundum Gregorium, in monilibus auro gemmæ imponuntur. Per aurum sapientia, per gemmas virtuosa et exemplaria opera designantur. Quum itaque prælatos oporteat per sapientiam rutilare, virtuosis quoque et exemplaribus actibus abundare, congrue monilia nuncupantur. Certum est etiam, per aurum posse intelligi caritatem: quæ sic eminet inter virtutes, sicut aurum inter metalla. Et sicut aurum habet vim lætificandi inspicientem, tristitiamque depellit, sic caritas maxime facit mentem in sponso super omnia caro gaudere, et ejus beatitudini intime congaudere. De qua in Apocalypsi legitur: Suadeo tibi emere aurum ignitum probatum. Per gemmas vero, pretiosissima illa septem dona Spiritus Sancti sumuntur. Prælatum autem oportet præ ceteris in caritate fervere, ac septenario Spiritus Sancti fulgere. Propter quod Christus beatissimum Petrum constituturus prælatum totius Ecclesiæ, ter sciscitatus est eum: Petre, amas me plus his? Hinc prælati dicuntur monilia. Erubescat ergo prælatus vocari, qui non satagit his ornatibus decorari: qui vel operari omittit quod docet, aut docere negligit quod a subditis suis Deus requirit. Nempe, ut ait Isidorus, tam vita quam doctrina clarescere debet in eo qui præsidet : quia doctrina sine vita efficit arrogantem, et vita sine doctrina inutilem. Pastoris sermo operibus est firmandus, ut quod instruit verbo, confirmet exemplo: turpissimum est, quempiam doctrinam suam propriis reprobare operibus.
paras.en: Further, according to Gregory, in jewels gems are set in gold. By the gold is signified wisdom, by the gems virtuous and exemplary works. Since, then, prelates must shine with wisdom and abound in virtuous and exemplary deeds, they are fittingly called jewels. It is certain also that by gold can be understood charity, which stands out among the virtues as gold does among the metals. And as gold has the power of gladdening the one who looks on it, and drives away sadness, so charity above all makes the mind rejoice in the Bridegroom, dear above all things, and rejoice inwardly in his beatitude. Of it we read in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 3:18|I counsel thee to buy of me gold, fire tried|Suadeo tibi emere aurum ignitum probatum]]. By the gems, again, are meant those most precious seven gifts of the Holy Ghost. Now a prelate must burn with charity more than the rest, and shine with the sevenfold Spirit. For this reason Christ, when about to make most blessed Peter prelate of the whole Church, asked him three times[[John 21:16||]][[John 21:17||]]: Peter, [[John 21:15|lovest thou me more than these|amas me plus his]]? Hence prelates are called jewels. Let him blush, then, to be called a prelate who does not take care to be adorned with these ornaments: who either fails to do what he teaches, or neglects to teach what God requires of his subjects. For, as Isidore says, he who presides ought to shine both in life and in doctrine: because doctrine without life makes a man arrogant, and life without doctrine makes him useless. The pastor's word must be made firm by his works, so that what he teaches by word he may confirm by example: it is most shameful for anyone to disprove his own doctrine by his own works.

paras.t: At vero per cervicem seu collum, Origenes intelligit membra Ecclesiæ bene subjecta, et obedientiæ dedita. Cervicibus enim onera deferenda solent imponi: propter quod, rebelles et inobedientes dicuntur esse duræ cervicis, et collo male erecto incedere. Unde per Prophetam Dominus ait: Scivi quia durus es tu, et nervus ferreus cervix tua, et frons tua ærea. Hinc ad insinuandum quod per collum obedientia designetur, Jeremias plurimos hortabatur, Subjicite colla vestra jugo regis Babylonis: quanto magis subjicienda sunt colla nostra jugo Christi, dicentis, Tollite jugum meum super vos! Hujus colli ornamenta, sunt sanctæ obedientiæ præstantissima opera. Unde quum quidam sanctorum Patrum vidisset in spiritu diversos ordines ministrantium Deo, ipsos religiosos sub obedientia viventes vidit aureos torques portare.
paras.en: But by the nape or neck Origen understands the members of the Church who are well subject and given to obedience. For burdens that are to be carried are usually laid on the neck: hence rebels and the disobedient are said to be stiff-necked[[Ex 32:9||]] and to walk with the neck ill held up. Hence the Lord says through the Prophet: [[Is 48:4|I knew that thou art stubborn, and thy neck is as an iron sinew, and thy forehead as brass|Scivi quia durus es tu, et nervus ferreus cervix tua, et frons tua ærea]]. Hence, to intimate that obedience is signified by the neck, Jeremias urged very many: [[Jer 27:12|Bend down your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon|Subjicite colla vestra jugo regis Babylonis]]: how much more must our necks be put under the yoke of Christ, who says: [[Matt 11:29|Take up my yoke upon you|Tollite jugum meum super vos]]! The ornaments of this neck are the most excellent works of holy obedience. Hence, when one of the holy Fathers saw in spirit the various orders of those who serve God, he saw the religious who live under obedience wearing golden collars.

paras.t: Murænulas aureas faciemus tibi, vermiculatas argento. Muræna (ut legitur) piscis est, in foramine suo existens circulatus et conglobatus: quia dum capitur, caudam ori suo imponit, et circulum de se facit; et sustentatur non comedendo, sed humorem sugendo: ad cujus similitudinem fiunt murænulæ, id est inaures, quæ aurium sunt ornatus. Gregorius vero dicit, quod per murænulas monilia ligantur ad collum. Atque, ut aliqui dicunt, murænulæ sunt ornamenta ex filis aureis et argenteis opere plectili facta, quibus ornantur capita feminarum, et oræ vestium circa manus et collum.
paras.en: [[1:10|We will make thee chains of gold, inlaid with silver|Murænulas aureas faciemus tibi, vermiculatas argento]] [the word rendered "chains" is *murænulæ*, "little morays", from *muræna*, the moray or lamprey, as Denis goes on to explain]. The muræna (as one reads) is a fish that lives in its hole coiled and rolled up: for when it is caught it puts its tail into its mouth and makes a circle of itself; and it is kept alive not by eating but by sucking in moisture. In its likeness are made *murænulæ*, that is, earrings, which are the ornaments of the ears. Gregory, however, says that by *murænulæ* necklaces are fastened to the neck. And, as some say, *murænulæ* are ornaments made of threads of gold and silver in plaited work, with which women's heads are adorned, and the edges of garments about the hands and the neck.

paras.t: Sicque per murænulas intelliguntur dogmata Scripturarum ac sententiæ Patrum, grandi decore permixta, sapientiam continentia, ac amore sancto flammigera, utpote igneæ legis verba: quæ murænulæ sunt vermiculatæ argento, id est venustate eloquentiæ hinc inde distinctæ, et varietate florum sui eloquii intermixtæ, ita quod in prædicatione et exhortatione sonant egregie, in tantum quod cordis secreta attingunt, compungunt, inflammant. Siquidem per argentum, nitor eloquii et sonoritas verbi in Scripturis signantur. Amplius, sicut in Scripturis per aurum, sapientia, id est notitia Dei, exprimitur; sic per argentum, scientia de rebus creatis notatur. Quum ergo Scriptura sacra non solum de Creatore, sed etiam de creaturis vere nos instruat, murænulæ, id est præfatæ divinorum sententiæ ac doctrinæ, recte dicuntur argento vermiculatæ. Has murænulas sponsus et ejus opifices (id est sacræ Scripturæ auctores) fecerunt Ecclesiæ, ut prædicaret ex eis, filiis suis ac subditis.
paras.en: And so by the chains are understood the doctrines of the Scriptures and the sentences of the Fathers, mingled with great beauty, containing wisdom, and aflame with holy love, as being the words of a fiery law: which chains are [[1:10|inlaid with silver|vermiculatæ argento]] [*vermiculatæ*, literally "worked in little worms", that is, inlaid in a varied pattern], that is, set off here and there with the beauty of eloquence, and interspersed with the variety of the flowers of their speech, so that in preaching and exhortation they sound out excellently, so much that they reach the secrets of the heart, prick it with compunction and inflame it. For by silver are signified in the Scriptures the brightness of speech and the resonance of the word. Further, as in the Scriptures wisdom, that is, the knowledge of God, is expressed by gold, so by silver is denoted knowledge of created things [*sapientia* and *scientia*: wisdom of divine things, knowledge of creatures]. Since, then, sacred Scripture instructs us truly not only about the Creator but also about creatures, the chains, that is, the aforesaid sentences and doctrines of divine things, are rightly said to be [[1:10|inlaid with silver|argento vermiculatæ]]. These chains the Bridegroom and his craftsmen (that is, the authors of sacred Scripture) have made for the Church, that she might preach from them to her sons and subjects.

paras.t: Dum esset rex in accubitu suo, nardus mea dedit odorem suum. Rex regum, Christus Dominus, morte devicta, ascendit ad Patrem, et requiescit ad dexteram ejus: atque ex tunc nardus sponsæ, id est ejus humilitas, vel salubris doctrina, ac suavissima fama, virtusque operativa miraculorum, dedit præcipue suum odorem, et redolentia sua multos attraxit, curavit, atque salvavit. In cujus odoris figura, Isaac dixit de filio suo: Ecce odor filii mei, sicut odor agri pleni. Denique sponso hoc corporaliter recumbente in domo Pharisæi, affectuosissima ejus discipula, optima illa Maria Magdalene, aromaticum suum unguentum nardi spicati pretiosi fudit super eumdem; et domus impleta est ex odore unguenti.
paras.en: [[1:11|While the king was at his repose, my spikenard sent forth the odour thereof.|Dum esset rex in accubitu suo, nardus mea dedit odorem suum]] The King of kings, Christ the Lord, having overcome death, ascended to the Father and rests at his right hand[[Mark 16:19||]]: and from then on the spikenard of the Bride, that is, her humility, or her wholesome doctrine, and her most sweet fame, and the power of working miracles, sent forth its odour above all, and by its fragrance drew many, healed them, and saved them. In figure of this odour Isaac said of his son: [[Gen 27:27|Behold, the smell of my son is as the smell of a plentiful field|Ecce odor filii mei, sicut odor agri pleni]]. Lastly, when this Bridegroom was reclining in the body in the house of the Pharisee, his most loving disciple, that excellent Mary Magdalene, poured upon him her aromatic [[Mark 14:3|ointment of precious spikenard|unguentum nardi spicati pretiosi]]; and [[John 12:3|the house was filled with the odour of the ointment|domus impleta est ex odore unguenti]] [Mark and John set this anointing in Bethania, Mark in the house of Simon the leper; the anointing in the Pharisee's house is that of Luke 7:36–38].

paras.t: Fasciculus myrrhæ, dilectus meus mihi. Myrrha amara est, et a putrefactione corpus præservat. Sicque sponsa duplici ratione dilectum suum vocat fasciculum myrrhæ: Primo, propter acerbitatem suæ salvificæ passionis, quam tulit pro nobis, ut sit sensus: Sponsus meus carissimus, propter ea quæ pro salute mea sustinuit, est mihi materia amaræ compassionis, et causa ob quam multiplici dolore me ipsam conficio in pœnitentiæ actibus et lamentis, in vigiliis, disciplinis, laboribus, abstinentiis, in fame, siti et frigore, in deploratione peccantium, in anxia adspiratione ad sponsum: ita quod lacrimæ meæ sunt mihi panes die ac nocte, præ desiderio plenæ fruitionis ac claræ visionis ipsius, me cupiente dissolvi et esse cum ipso. Secundo sic: Fasciculus myrrhæ, id est copiosa medicina contra putredinem vitiorum, et curativa præteritarum culparum, est dilectus meus mihi: qui suis documentis, præceptis, consiliis, infusioneque gratiæ ac virtutum, et ecclesiasticis sacramentis ac virtutum suarum exemplis, præbet remedia contra omnia vulnera vitiorum; qui primo in Baptismo, deinde in Confessione, ab omni mundat et curat inquinamento.
paras.en: [[1:12|A bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me|Fasciculus myrrhæ, dilectus meus mihi]]. Myrrh is bitter, and preserves the body from corruption. And so the Bride calls her beloved a bundle of myrrh for two reasons. First, because of the bitterness of his saving passion, which he bore for us; so that the sense is: My dearest Bridegroom, because of what he endured for my salvation, is to me matter of bitter compassion, and the cause for which I wear myself out with manifold sorrow in acts of penance and in laments, in vigils, disciplines [that is, scourgings taken as penance], labours and fastings, in hunger, thirst and cold, in weeping for sinners, in anxious longing for the Bridegroom: so that [[Ps 41:4|My tears have been my bread day and night|lacrimæ meæ sunt mihi panes die ac nocte]], for desire of the full enjoyment and clear vision of him, as I long [[Phil 1:23|to be dissolved and to be with|dissolvi et esse cum]] him. Secondly thus: [[1:12|A bundle of myrrh|Fasciculus myrrhæ]], that is, an abundant medicine against the rottenness of vices, and a healing of past faults, [[1:12|is my beloved to me|est dilectus meus mihi]]: who by his teachings, precepts and counsels, by the infusion of grace and the virtues, and by the sacraments of the Church and the examples of his virtues, provides remedies against all the wounds of vices; who first in Baptism, then in Confession, cleanses and heals from all defilement.

paras.t: Ideo, inter ubera mea commorabitur: id est, in intimis præcordiorum meorum quiescet; et nequaquam obliviscar ipsius, sed in omni necessitate, tentatione, angustia et ruina ad ipsum confugiam, inter prospera et adversa intra me eum amplectar, eum orando, psallendo, meditando affabor. Et sicut ejus intuitu ac amore, omnem carnalem delectationem vilemque consolationem et dissolutionem puerilem despicio; ita ex ejus contemplatione, omnem inordinatum mœrorem ac mordacem tristitiam fugo ac vinco: ut nec prosperitate dissolvar, nec adversitatibus frangar. Quæ enim tribulatio me poterit superare, dum quæ et quanta ipse pro me toleravit, intueor? Humilitas ejus, mihi medicamentum est contra omnem superbiæ læsionem; consideratio patientiæ ac mansuetudinis ejus, omnem iracundiæ impetum curat, omnem impatientiam tollit; fervor suæ ardentissimæ caritatis, cunctam repellit pigritiam et teporem. Denique inter ubera mea commorabitur, quia in omni doctrina et utriusque Testamenti Scripturis ipsius recordabor, et sermocinabor de eo. Universa quoque quæ pro mea assumpsit, fecit, pertulitque salute, colligabo quasi in unum fasciculum: quem jugiter intuebor, quatenus incarnatio, conversatio ac passio dilectissimi sponsi mei nunquam a mea recedat memoria, juxta illud in Threnis: Memoria memor ero, et tabescet in me anima mea. Ut sic cum Apostolo dicere queam: Christo confixus sum cruci. Vivo autem jam non ego: vivit vero in me Christus. Et denuo: Mihi autem absit gloriari, nisi in cruce Domini mei Jesu Christi. Est namque in cruce sponsi gloriatio, dum gloriamur in hoc, quod ejus amore et imitatione adversum quid patimur, et contumelias sustinemus; et rursus, dum passionem ipsius tam fructuosissimam esse perpendimus, quod per eam reconciliati sumus Deo omnipotenti, et liberati a discrimine infernali.
paras.en: Therefore [[1:12|he shall abide between my breasts|inter ubera mea commorabitur]]: that is, he shall rest in the inmost depths of my heart; and I will never forget him, but in every need, temptation, distress and fall I will flee to him; amid prosperity and adversity I will embrace him within me, and speak with him by praying, by psalmody, by meditating. And as, by looking on him and by love of him, I despise all carnal delight, base consolation and childish dissipation, so by contemplating him I put to flight and overcome all inordinate grief and gnawing sadness, so that I am neither unstrung by prosperity nor broken by adversities. For what tribulation will be able to overcome me, while I behold what and how great things he bore for me? His humility is my medicine against every wound of pride; the consideration of his patience and meekness heals every onset of anger and takes away all impatience; the fervour of his most burning charity drives off all sloth and lukewarmness. Again, [[1:12|he shall abide between my breasts|inter ubera mea commorabitur]], because in all doctrine and in the Scriptures of both Testaments I will remember him and speak of him. All that he took on, did and bore for my salvation I will also bind together as into one bundle, on which I will gaze continually, so that the incarnation, the life and the passion of my most beloved Bridegroom may never depart from my memory, according to that in Lamentations: [[Lam 3:20|I will be mindful and remember, and my soul shall languish within me|Memoria memor ero, et tabescet in me anima mea]]. So that thus I may say with the Apostle: [[Gal 2:19|with Christ I am nailed to the cross|Christo confixus sum cruci]]. [[Gal 2:20|And I live, now not I: but Christ liveth in me|Vivo autem jam non ego: vivit vero in me Christus]]. And again: [[Gal 6:14|But God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross|Mihi autem absit gloriari, nisi in cruce]] of my Lord Jesus Christ. For there is glorying in the cross of the Bridegroom when we glory in this, that for love and imitation of him we suffer something adverse and endure insults; and again, when we consider his passion to be so very fruitful, that by it [[Rom 5:10|we were reconciled to God|reconciliati sumus Deo]] almighty, and were delivered from the peril of hell[[Rom 5:11||]].

paras.t: Ideo subditur: Botrus Cypri, dilectus meus mihi in vineis Engaddi: id est, ipse qui in passione sua factus est mihi fasciculus myrrhæ, in sua resurrectione, ascensione, et Spiritus Sancti missione, atque in quotidiana sua gratiosa visitatione ac consolatione interna, factus est mihi botrus Cypri, id est materia exhilarationis, spiritualeque vinum inebrians mentem fervore amoris, plenitudine devotionis, exuberantia internæ suavitatis: quod totum recte per botrum Cypri insinuatur, quia in insula Cypro vinum optimum generatur. Sic demum factus est mihi botrus in vineis Engaddi, id est loci sic dicti, quæ et ipsæ optimæ esse feruntur. Engaddi vero, fons hœdi interpretatur. Hœdus autem fuit in lege animal immolaticium pro remissione culparum. Idcirco per hœdum peccatores signantur; et per fontem hœdi, Baptismus seu Pœnitentiæ sacramentum, in quibus iniqui a suis peccatis lavantur: sicque sponsus est sponsæ suæ botrus in vineis Engaddi, hoc est in Ecclesiis renatorum in fonte Baptismatis, seu purgatorum in sacramento Confessionis.
paras.en: Therefore it is added: [[1:13|A cluster of cypress my love is to me, in the vineyards of Engaddi|Botrus Cypri, dilectus meus mihi in vineis Engaddi]]: that is, he who in his passion became to me a bundle of myrrh, in his resurrection, his ascension and the sending of the Holy Ghost, and in his daily gracious visitation and inward consolation, has become to me a cluster of Cyprus, that is, matter of gladness, and a spiritual wine inebriating the mind with the fervour of love, with fullness of devotion, with overflowing inward sweetness: all of which is rightly suggested by the cluster of Cyprus [Denis here reads *cypri* as the island of Cyprus; below he gives the other reading, *cyprus* the shrub], because the best wine is produced in the island of Cyprus. So, lastly, he has become to me a cluster [[1:13|in the vineyards of Engaddi|in vineis Engaddi]], that is, of the place so called, whose vineyards too are said to be the best. Now Engaddi is interpreted *fountain of the kid*. And the kid was in the law an animal sacrificed for the remission of faults[[Ex 12:5||]]. Therefore by the kid sinners are signified, and by the fountain of the kid Baptism or the sacrament of Penance, in which the wicked are washed from their sins: and so the Bridegroom is to his Bride a cluster in the vineyards of Engaddi, that is, in the Churches of those reborn in the font of Baptism, or cleansed in the sacrament of Confession.

paras.t: Denique, quia sub speciebus panis et vini, sponsa dilectum suum quotidie sumit in sacro Mysterio, recte eum comparat botro: de quo sponso in libro Geneseos Jacob patriarcha vaticinatur: Ligans ad vineam pullum suum, et ad vitem, o fili mi, asinam suam: lavabit in vino stolam suam, et in sanguine uvæ pallium suum. Ideo in ejus ascensione sciscitati sunt angeli sancti: Quare rubrum est indumentum tuum, et vestimenta tua sicut calcantium in torculari? Quibus respondet: Torcular calcavi solus. Christus quippe est botrus, de quo in torculari passionis, id est patibulo crucis, expressum est optimum vinum, utpote sanguis salvificus in Sacramento reficiens, lætificans, inebrians communicantem. De quo sancto edulio, salutarique poculo, in alio Propheta scriptum est: Quid bonum Domini, aut quid pulchrum ejus, nisi frumentum electorum, et vinum germinans virgines? Unde de hoc sponso, prophetatum fuit in Psalmo: Erit firmamentum in terra in summis montium. Ubi pro firmamento, alia littera habet, Frumentum; alia vero, Memoriale triticum. Imo translatio Chaldaica aptissime habet, Erit placenta tritici: quia videlicet Christus sub forma tortulæ seu placentæ triticeæ, offertur quotidie Deo Patri in celebratione.
paras.en: Lastly, because under the species of bread and wine the Bride receives her beloved daily in the sacred Mystery, she rightly compares him to a cluster: of which Bridegroom the patriarch Jacob prophesies in the book of Genesis: [[Gen 49:11|Tying his foal to the vineyard, and his ass, O my son, to the vine. He shall wash his robe in wine, and his garment in the blood of the grape.|Ligans ad vineam pullum suum, et ad vitem, o fili mi, asinam suam: lavabit in vino stolam suam, et in sanguine uvæ pallium suum]] Therefore at his ascension the holy angels asked: [[Is 63:2|Why then is thy apparel red, and thy garments like theirs that tread in the winepress?|Quare rubrum est indumentum tuum, et vestimenta tua sicut calcantium in torculari?]] To whom he answers: [[Is 63:3|I have trodden the winepress alone|Torcular calcavi solus]]. For Christ is the cluster from which, in the winepress of the passion, that is, on the gibbet of the cross, the best wine was pressed out, namely the saving blood, which in the Sacrament refreshes, gladdens and inebriates the communicant. Of which holy food and saving cup it is written in another Prophet: [[Zach 9:17|what is the good thing of him, and what is his beautiful thing, but the corn of the elect, and wine springing forth virgins?|Quid bonum Domini, aut quid pulchrum ejus, nisi frumentum electorum, et vinum germinans virgines?]] Hence it was prophesied of this Bridegroom in the Psalm: [[Ps 71:16|there shall be a firmament on the earth on the tops of mountains|Erit firmamentum in terra in summis montium]]. Where for *firmament* one text has *Corn*, and another *A memorial of wheat*. Indeed the Chaldee translation has most aptly, *There shall be a cake of wheat*: because, that is, Christ under the form of a little cake or wafer of wheat is offered daily to God the Father in the celebration [that is, of Mass].

paras.t: Præterea aliqui dicunt, quod Engaddi est locus in quo balsamum crescit, et arbor aromatica nomine cyprus, quæ facit grana similia granis uvæ, atque in modum vitis excolitur, propter quod vinea nominatur: sicque Cyprus, non esset hic nomen insulæ in mari Mediterraneo sitæ, de qua Barnabas fuit apostolus. Hinc ait et Origenes: Uva florens, cyprus vocatur. Species quoque extrinsecus est cujusdam virgulti, quæ dicitur cyprus, producens fructum in modum uvæ florentis. Sed videtur magis ad fructum vitis sermo respicere, quia vinearum Engaddi est facta memoria. Engaddi autem ager est terræ Judææ, non tantum vineis quantum balsamis florens. Sponsa ergo adolescentulis loquens: Botrus (inquit) cypri, dilectus meus mihi. Tanquam dicat, Quidquid dulcedinis in odoribus est et floribus virgultorum, superat sponsus: quatenus audientes hæc adolescentulæ, magis ac magis ad sponsi concitentur amorem.
paras.en: Moreover some say that Engaddi is a place in which balsam grows, and an aromatic tree by the name of *cyprus*, which bears berries like the grapes of a vine and is cultivated in the manner of a vine, for which reason it is called a vineyard: and so *Cyprus* would not here be the name of the island situated in the Mediterranean Sea, from which the apostle Barnabas came[[Acts 4:36||]]. Hence Origen too says: The flowering grape is called *cyprus*. There is also, besides, a species of a certain shrub which is called *cyprus*, producing fruit in the manner of a flowering grape. But the words seem rather to look to the fruit of the vine, since mention is made of the vineyards of Engaddi. Engaddi, however, is a field of the land of Judea, flourishing not so much with vineyards as with balsams. The Bride, then, speaking to the maidens: [[1:13|A cluster|Botrus]] (she says) [[1:13|of cypress my love is to me|cypri, dilectus meus mihi]]. As if she said: Whatever sweetness there is in the odours and flowers of shrubs, the Bridegroom surpasses it: so that the maidens, hearing this, may be stirred more and more to the love of the Bridegroom.

paras.t: Insuper videns sponsus universalem Ecclesiam suo desiderio æstuantem, ac suis præconiis inhærentem, imo et aliorum animas sua caritate affectuosis sermonibus inflammantem, prorumpit in laudem ipsius, ut ad meliora provocet eam. Ecce tu pulchra es, amica mea, ecce tu pulchra. Repetitio ista, affirmationis, affectionis, seriositatis, ac movendæ attentionis est signum, quasi dicat: Tu, sponsa mea, sancta et præelecta Ecclesia, pro qua tradidi me in mortem, tu pulchra es mente et corporis castitate. Pulchra per dona naturæ, pulchrior per charismata gratiæ. Pulchra interius, per virtutum et donorum meritorumque claritates; pulchra extrinsecus, per venustissimos mores. Pulchra sacramentorum decore, ornata ministrorum tuorum multiplici distinctione, prælatorum et religiosorum atque doctorum multiformi gradu, statu, ac ordine; decorata non solum donis supernaturalibus gratiæ gratum facientis, sed etiam gratiæ gratis datæ. De quibus omnibus multisque aliis sponsæ hujus ornatibus, in epistolis ad Corinthios et Ephesios copiose disseruit sapientissimus Paulus. Et sicut in libris de Angelica atque Ecclesiastica hierarchiis divinus testatur Dionysius, Ecclesia seu ecclesiastica hierarchia, instar hierarchiæ angelicæ exstat disposita. Propter quod Joannes in Apocalypsi fatetur: Vidi civitatem sanctam, Jerusalem novam, descendentem de cœlo, a Deo paratam, tanquam sponsam ornatam viro suo, habentem claritatem Dei.
paras.en: Further, the Bridegroom, seeing the universal Church burning with desire for him and clinging to his praises, and indeed inflaming the souls of others with his charity by loving words, breaks out in her praise, to provoke her to better things: [[1:14|Behold thou are fair, O my love, behold thou are fair|Ecce tu pulchra es, amica mea, ecce tu pulchra]]. This repetition is a sign of affirmation, of affection, of earnestness, and of rousing attention; as if he said: Thou, my Bride, holy and chosen Church, for whom I delivered myself to death[[Eph 5:25||]], thou art fair in mind and in chastity of body. Fair by the gifts of nature, fairer by the charisms of grace. Fair within, by the splendours of virtues, gifts and merits; fair without, by most comely manners. Fair with the beauty of the sacraments, adorned with the manifold distinction of thy ministers, with the many grades, states and orders of prelates, religious and doctors; adorned not only with the supernatural gifts of sanctifying grace [*gratia gratum faciens*, the grace that makes one pleasing to God] but also with those of graces freely given [*gratiæ gratis datæ*, such as prophecy or healing, given for the good of others]. Of all these and many other adornments of this Bride the most wise Paul discoursed copiously in the epistles to the Corinthians and the Ephesians[[1 Cor 12:1||]][[Eph 4:11||]][[Eph 5:27||]] [the margin gives 1 Cor. xii; Ephes. iv, 11; v, 25–27]. And as the divine Dionysius testifies in his books on the Angelic and the Ecclesiastical Hierarchies, the Church, or ecclesiastical hierarchy, stands ordered after the likeness of the angelic hierarchy. Wherefore John declares in the Apocalypse: I [[Apoc 21:2|saw the holy city, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband|Vidi civitatem sanctam, Jerusalem novam, descendentem de cœlo, a Deo paratam, tanquam sponsam ornatam viro suo]][[Apoc 21:10||]], [[Apoc 21:11|Having the glory of God|habentem claritatem Dei]].

paras.t: Oculi tui columbarum: id est, columbina simplicitate, sincera intentione, acuto ac limpido ad contemplandum intuitu fulges; longe a te omnis hypocrisis, omnis duplicitas cordis, omnis perversa intentio; me solum habes præ oculis, ad meum honorem et gloriam omnia refers; non respicis ad commoda tua privata, sed imples quod jussi, Estote prudentes sicut serpentes, et simplices sicut columbæ. Etenim advertisti quod dixi: Si oculus tuus fuerit simplex, totum corpus tuum lucidum erit. Non es vaga aut lasciva, sed faceta, custodita, pudibunda adspectu, sicut honestissimam condecet sponsam: quæ erubescit in alienum sponsum figere visum, imo nec proprium, nisi cum modestia, intuetur: per quod bono contorali non mediocriter placet. Præterea multæ sunt proprietates columbæ, propter quas ei assimilatur et comparatur Ecclesia: de quibus modo pertranseo, quoniam infra magis super hoc se offeret sermo.
paras.en: [[1:14|thy eyes are as those of doves|Oculi tui columbarum]]: that is, thou shinest with dovelike simplicity, with sincere intention, with a keen and clear gaze for contemplation; far from thee is all hypocrisy, all doubleness of heart, every perverse intention; thou hast me alone before thine eyes, thou referrest all things to my honour and glory; thou lookest not to thine own private advantage, but fulfillest what I commanded: [[Matt 10:16|Be ye therefore wise as serpents and simple as doves|Estote prudentes sicut serpentes, et simplices sicut columbæ]]. For thou hast heeded what I said: [[Matt 6:22|If thy eye be single, thy whole body shall be lightsome|Si oculus tuus fuerit simplex, totum corpus tuum lucidum erit]] [*simplex*, "single", is also "simple", as the doves are]. Thou art not wandering or wanton, but gracious, guarded, modest in thy look, as becomes a most honourable bride: who blushes to fix her gaze on a strange bridegroom, and indeed does not look even on her own except with modesty; whereby she pleases her good consort not a little.
