Sometimes also it is done to belittle, and at times to suggest in something else the degree of its smallness or inferiority. Again, it is called a little bed to signify the immensity of this bridegroom: for compared with so great a bridegroom every place where he can rest, even a spiritual one, is small. Hence we read in Isaias too: [[Is 28:20|the bed is straitened|Coangustatum est stratum]]. What this little bed is has been said in the preceding article.

paras.t: Tigna domorum nostrarum cedrina, laquearia cypressina. Domus spiritualis, in qua sponsus supernus cum anima demoratur, est virtutum structura, et coordinatio atque connexio earumdem. In qua domo fides, seu timor Dei, sive humilitas est fundamentum; pavimentum vero, est virtutum moralium ordinata locatio, quarum est passiones reprimere. Primum autem solarium, est virtutum intellectualium superlocatio: quibus dona pro secundo superponuntur solario. Spes autem et caritas Dei ac proximi, cum actibus suis, tigna sunt, totam prætactam virtutum structuram sustentantia et consolidantia; laquearia vero seu testudines, quæ implent atque decorant domum, sunt sanctæ meditationes, virtuosæque affectiones, octo beatitudines, et duodecim fructus. Præterea virtutes theologicæ faciunt domum spiritualem per se: similiter virtutes morales, et item intellectuales. Imo unaquæque virtus per gradus et actus, delectationes ac merita sua, efficit domum suam, in qua sponsus moratur cum sponsa: quælibet etenim virtus habet pro pavimento gradum infimum, quo competit statui incipientium; gradum medium, quo convenit statui proficientium; gradumque summum, quo statui congruit perfectorum. Denique spiritualia tigna et laquearia ista, cedrina dicuntur et cypressina: quoniam boni odoris et laudabilis famæ sunt diffusiva, et ex se immaterialia bona, a corruptione vitii aliena, infernalium serpentium expulsiva: prout hæc ex præhabita expositione clarius queunt elici ac patere.
paras.en: [[1:16|The beams of our houses are of cedar, our rafters of cypress trees|Tigna domorum nostrarum cedrina, laquearia cypressina]]. The spiritual house in which the heavenly bridegroom dwells with the soul is the structure of the virtues, their ordering together and their joining. In this house faith, or the fear of God, or humility, is the foundation; the floor is the ordered placing of the moral virtues, whose work is to restrain the passions. The first upper storey [*solarium*, an upper floor or loft] is the setting above them of the intellectual virtues: and over these the gifts [of the Holy Ghost] are set as the second storey. Hope and charity towards God and neighbour, with their acts, are the beams, which hold up and make firm the whole structure of the virtues just described; and the rafters or vaults [*laquearia*, the panelled ceiling], which fill out and adorn the house, are holy meditations, virtuous affections, the eight beatitudes and the twelve fruits. Further, the theological virtues by themselves make a spiritual house; so likewise do the moral virtues, and so too the intellectual. Indeed each single virtue, by its degrees and acts, its delights and merits, makes its own house, in which the bridegroom dwells with the bride: for every virtue has for its floor the lowest degree, which befits the state of beginners; a middle degree, which suits the state of those making progress; and the highest degree, which suits the state of the perfect. Lastly, these spiritual beams and rafters are said to be of cedar and of cypress because they spread abroad a good odour and a praiseworthy fame, and are of themselves immaterial goods, strangers to the corruption of vice, and drive away the serpents of hell [cedar and cypress were held to be incorruptible and to keep off serpents by their scent]: as may be drawn out and made plain more clearly from the exposition given before.

1.title: DECLARATIO EJUSDEM CAPITULI PRIMI, DE SPONSA SINGULARI.
1.title_en: Declaration of the same first chapter: of the singular Bride

paras.t: SPONSA singularis et singulariter unica atque ineffabiliter prædilecta sponsi cœlestis, est virginea, purissima ac sacratissima Mater ipsius, ab ipso sponso unigenito Filio suo fide illuminatissima desponsata, spe certissima subarrhata, caritate ferventissima amplexata, copiosissime fecundata per exuberantissima gratiarum charismata. Hinc Cantica ista in hujus solennitatibus sponsæ, in divino leguntur Officio. Breviter ergo tangendum est, qualiter ei conveniant.
paras.en: The singular bride of the heavenly Bridegroom, singularly the only one and beloved before all others beyond words, is His virginal, most pure and most holy Mother: espoused by that Bridegroom, her only-begotten Son, in a most enlightened faith, pledged to Him [that is, betrothed with an earnest or pledge, *subarrhata*] in a most certain hope, embraced in a most fervent charity, and made most abundantly fruitful by the overflowing gifts of graces. Hence these Canticles are read in the divine Office on the feasts of this bride. We must therefore touch briefly on how they befit her.

paras.t: Denique de gloriosissima et incomparabili Virgine ista dignissima, ab æterno præelecta in veram Matrem veri Dei, certa fide tenendum censetur, quod multo excellentius fuit sanctificata ac Spiritu Sancto repleta in utero suæ matris, quam gloriosus Joannes Baptista, de quo Gabriel angelus prænuntiavit : Spiritu Sancto replebitur adhuc ex utero matris suæ; aut Jeremias, cui locutus est Dominus, Priusquam formarem te in utero, novi te, et antequam exires de ventre, sanctificavi te; aut quispiam aliorum, si qui forte in utero sanctificati fuerunt, ipso incomparabiliter sancto sponso excepto. Et sicut incomparabilis atque mundissima Virgo, fuit præ cunctis in utero matris supernis charismatibus adimpleta; ita mox ut ratione uti cœpit, assidue in eisdem præ omnibus illis profecit : sicque quo excellentiori puritate mens ejus præelecta coram Altissimo radiavit, et quo ad proficiendum in omni virtute ac sapientia vigilantior, instantior, seriosior fuit, eo eminentius ac munificentius omni hora a Spiritu Sancto ungebatur, illuminabatur, accendebatur, et incomparabiliter crevit ; et quo specialius fuit ex Deo, eo avidius Dei verba advertit, fuitque studiosa et erudita in lege. Ac, sicut testatur Ambrosius, ipsa legit (haud dubium quin in Isaia) : Ecce virgo concipiet. Imo, ut ex Scripturis colligitur, antequam Filium Dei concepit, noverat superbeatissimæ Trinitatis mysterium, id est, trinitatem Personarum esse in Deo. Quum enim interrogasset ab angelo, Quomodo fiet istud, quoniam virum non cognosco? responsum est ei ore angelico : Spiritus Sanctus superveniet in te, et virtus Altissimi obumbrabit tibi. Ideoque et quod nascetur ex te Sanctum, vocabitur Filius Dei. In quibus adoranda Trinitas manifeste insinuatur. Quam utique responsionem ipsa intellexit.
paras.en: Now concerning this most glorious, incomparable and most worthy Virgin, chosen from eternity to be the true Mother of the true God, it is judged that we must hold with sure faith that she was sanctified and filled with the Holy Ghost in her mother's womb far more excellently than the glorious John the Baptist, of whom the angel Gabriel foretold: [[Luke 1:15|he shall be filled with the Holy Ghost, even from his mother's womb|Spiritu Sancto replebitur adhuc ex utero matris suæ]]; or Jeremias, to whom the Lord said, [[Jer 1:5|Before I formed thee in the bowels of thy mother, I knew thee: and before thou camest forth out of the womb, I sanctified thee|Priusquam formarem te in utero, novi te, et antequam exires de ventre, sanctificavi te]]; or any of the others, if any others perhaps were sanctified in the womb, excepting only her incomparably holy Bridegroom Himself. And as the incomparable and most pure Virgin was filled in her mother's womb with heavenly gifts above all, so as soon as she began to use her reason she advanced in them continually beyond all those: and thus, the more excellent the purity with which her chosen mind shone before the Most High, and the more watchful, earnest and serious she was in advancing in every virtue and wisdom, the more eminently and bountifully was she anointed, enlightened and kindled by the Holy Ghost every hour, and she grew beyond compare; and the more especially she was of God, the more eagerly she heeded the words of God, and she was studious and learned in the law. And, as Ambrose testifies, she herself read (no doubt in Isaias): [[Is 7:14|Behold a virgin shall conceive|Ecce virgo concipiet]]. Indeed, as is gathered from the Scriptures, before she conceived the Son of God she knew the mystery of the most blessed Trinity, that is, that there is a trinity of Persons in God. For when she had asked the angel, [[Luke 1:34|How shall this be done, because I know not man?|Quomodo fiet istud, quoniam virum non cognosco?]] the answer given her from the angel's mouth was: [[Luke 1:35|The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee and the power of the Most High shall overshadow thee. And therefore also the Holy which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God|Spiritus Sanctus superveniet in te, et virtus Altissimi obumbrabit tibi. Ideoque et quod nascetur ex te Sanctum, vocabitur Filius Dei]]. In these words the adorable Trinity is plainly intimated; and she certainly understood this answer.

paras.t: Credendum ergo videtur, quod ex scripturis legis ac Prophetarum, potius vero ex familiari et interna unctione instructioneque Spiritus Sancti, jam noverat Deum, imo et unicum Dei Filium, incarnandum ac passurum ad redimendum genus humanum; nec dubium quin tanto affectuosius præ ceteris adventum tanti desideraverit Redemptoris, quanto in caritate æstuantior exstitit illis. Et quamvis præ inæstimabili et ex profundissima suæ tranquillissimæ mentis humilitate, nequaquam præsumpserit aut putaverit de se Dei Filium incarnandum, vel ad tanta mysteria se esse electam; nihilo minus, quum ex angelico cognovisset alloquio, se ad hoc esse electam, et Dei Filium concepturam, mox tacta a Spiritu Sancto, plenarie credidit, humillime quoque consensit, idque fieri ferventissime concupivit : Ecce, inquiens, ancilla Domini; fiat mihi secundum verbum tuum.
paras.en: It seems, then, that we must believe that from the writings of the Law and the Prophets, but still more from the familiar and inward anointing and teaching of the Holy Ghost, she already knew that God, indeed the only Son of God, was to become incarnate and to suffer in order to redeem the human race; and there is no doubt that she longed for the coming of so great a Redeemer with as much more affection than the others as she burned more ardently than they in charity. And although, out of the inestimable and most profound humility of her most tranquil mind, she never presumed or thought that the Son of God would become incarnate of her, or that she had been chosen for such mysteries, nevertheless, when she learned from the angel's address that she had been chosen for this and would conceive the Son of God, at once, touched by the Holy Ghost, she believed fully, consented most humbly, and most fervently desired that it be done, saying: [[Luke 1:38|Behold|Ecce]], [[Luke 1:38|the handmaid of the Lord: be it done to me according to thy word|ancilla Domini; fiat mihi secundum verbum tuum]].

paras.t: De ipsa igitur optima sapientissimaque Virguncula, ut constituta in illa hora, qua audivit ab angelo sancto, Ecce concipies in utero; et deinceps, Spiritus Sanctus superveniet in te, etc., congruentissime potest exponi quod dicitur : Osculetur me osculo oris sui : id est, Unigenitus Dei, sponsus cœlestis, quem tu, o paranymphe superne, mihi promittis, ex me incarnandum testaris, filium meum mox futurum affirmas, ad me ancillam suam parvulam dignetur descendere, seque substantiæ carnis meæ tam proxime et immediate conjungere, ut ex ea corpus sibi assumat ac hypostatice uniat, id est, suæ increatæ personalitati una cum anima rationali ab ipso creanda, et corpus hoc informatura, personali copulet unione : ut sic natura humana ad constituendam unam personam cum Verbo æterno, assumatur ab ipso Verbo, Dei Patris unico Filio. — Insuper, Osculetur me osculo oris sui : id est, tam amorose et proxime mentem meam luce sapientiæ suæ perfundat, accendat, et amplexetur, ut in hora ista idonea fiam ac sim concipere Dominum Deum creatorem ac salvatorem meum : quem carne concipere quid prodesset, nisi hunc prius mente conciperem? sicque beatior sim concipiendo fide formata, quam carne sola. Siquidem maternitas ista, seu Matrem Dei exsistere, donum est gratiæ gratis datæ : quod per se, habenti non sufficit ad salutem.
paras.en: Of this best and wisest little Virgin, then, as she stood in that hour in which she heard from the holy angel, [[Luke 1:31|Behold thou shalt conceive in thy womb|Ecce concipies in utero]], and then, [[Luke 1:35|The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee|Spiritus Sanctus superveniet in te]], etc., the words can most fittingly be expounded: [[1:1|Let him kiss me with the kiss of his mouth|Osculetur me osculo oris sui]]: that is, may the Only-begotten of God, the heavenly Bridegroom, whom thou, O heavenly paranymph [that is, groomsman, the friend who arranges the marriage], promisest me, whom thou declarest is to become incarnate of me, and affirmest is soon to be my son, deign to come down to me, His little handmaid, and to join Himself so closely and immediately to the substance of my flesh that He take a body from it and unite it to Himself hypostatically: that is, that He join it in personal union to His uncreated personality, together with a rational soul to be created by Him that will give form to this body; so that human nature may thus be assumed by the Word Himself, the only Son of God the Father, to make one person with the eternal Word. Moreover, [[1:1|Let him kiss me with the kiss of his mouth|Osculetur me osculo oris sui]]: that is, may He so lovingly and closely flood, kindle and embrace my mind with the light of His wisdom, that in this hour I may become and be fit to conceive the Lord God, my Creator and Saviour. For what would it profit me to conceive Him in the flesh, unless I first conceived Him in the mind? And so may I be more blessed in conceiving by faith formed [that is, faith living by charity] than in the flesh alone. For this motherhood, or being the Mother of God, is a gift of grace freely given [*gratia gratis data*: a grace given for the good of others, which does not of itself make its receiver holy], which by itself is not enough for the salvation of the one who has it.

paras.t: Præterea, Osculetur me osculo oris sui : id est, ipse quem cœlum et terra capere nequeunt, qui nullo valet termino circumscribi, nullo intellectu creato comprehendi, incarnatus ex me, mecum dulciter conversetur, meo gremio contineatur, inter mea brachia concludatur, meisque manibus contrectetur: et ita me osculetur osculo corporali sincerissimo serenissimi oris sui. Non enim ambigitur quin tu, affectuosissima mater, pudicissima virgo, unicum illum tui virginei uteri fructum, speciosissimum pretiosissimumque infantulum puerum, Deum ex te natum, tibi carissimum, interdum sis cum ingenti reverentia amplexata, cum caritate maxima osculata. Ipse quoque, qui in ætate virili suos consuevit ad se venientes discipulos cum osculo sancto recipere corporali, te utique in pueritia constitutus, tanquam dilectissimam genitricem, consuevit nonnunquam suaviter osculari, sanctumque collum tuum sacratissimis suis brachiolis stringere. Quod si beati oculi et aures discipulorum, qui Christum viderunt ac audierunt : quanto magis tu beata, quæ ipsum concepisti ac peperisti, atque maternis educasti obsequiis, ipsumque auctoritate materna tractare et deosculari valebas?
paras.en: Further, [[1:1|Let him kiss me with the kiss of his mouth|Osculetur me osculo oris sui]]: that is, may He whom heaven and earth cannot contain[[2 Par 2:6||]], who can be bounded by no limit and comprehended by no created understanding, become incarnate of me and sweetly dwell with me, be held in my lap, be enfolded in my arms and handled by my hands; and so may He kiss me with the most pure bodily kiss of His most serene mouth. For there is no doubt that thou, most affectionate mother, most chaste virgin, didst at times embrace with immense reverence and kiss with the greatest charity that only fruit of thy virginal womb, the most beautiful and precious little child, God born of thee and most dear to thee. He too, who in His manhood was wont to receive His disciples coming to Him with a holy bodily kiss, was certainly wont at times in His childhood to kiss thee sweetly, as His most beloved mother, and to clasp thy holy neck with His most sacred little arms. And if the eyes and ears of the disciples who saw and heard Christ were blessed[[Matt 13:16||]][[Luke 10:23||]], how much more blessed art thou, who didst conceive and bear Him, and bring Him up with a mother's care, and couldst handle and kiss Him with a mother's authority?

paras.t: Quia meliora sunt ubera tua vino, fragrantia unguentis optimis. Ista, juxta expositiones præhabitas, possunt esse verba sponsæ singularis ad unicum sponsum ac Filium suum : quæ sui Filii spiritualia ubera tanto specialius potuit commendare, quanto mens sua ab illis fuerat exquisitius, exuberantius, ac dulcius enutrita, uncta et consolata. Possunt quoque esse verba sponsi ad dilectissimam Matrem suam, ut sit sensus : Tu, o singularis sponsa, mater et virgo, osculum oris mei petisti, et ego tuæ petitioni libenter assentio, quia meliora sunt ubera tua vino : id est, caritas tua, qua zelo honoris tui Creatoris ferves, et proximos tuos orationibus atque exemplis foves; et pietas tua, qua pereuntibus condoles ac subvenire desideras : hæc, inquam, ubera tua, quibus me allicis, meliora sunt vino, id est legis rigore et omni corporali dulcore, fragrantia unguentis optimis, id est sublimi contemplatione, qua divinæ majestatis honorabilitatem interminabilem contemplaris, ac præclara discretione, qua cuncta ordinate decenterque peragis.
paras.en: [[1:1|for thy breasts are better than wine|Quia meliora sunt ubera tua vino]], [[1:2|Smelling sweet of the best ointments|fragrantia unguentis optimis]]. According to the expositions given before, these can be the words of the singular bride to her only Bridegroom and Son: she could praise her Son's spiritual breasts the more especially, the more exquisitely, abundantly and sweetly her mind had been nourished, anointed and consoled by them. They can also be the words of the Bridegroom to His most beloved Mother, so that the sense is: Thou, O singular bride, mother and virgin, hast asked for the kiss of My mouth, and I gladly grant thy request, [[1:1|for thy breasts are better than wine|Quia meliora sunt ubera tua vino]]: that is, thy charity, with which thou burnest with zeal for the honour of thy Creator and cherishest thy neighbours by thy prayers and examples; and thy compassion, with which thou grievest for those who are perishing and longest to help them: these, I say, thy breasts, with which thou drawest Me, are better than wine, that is, than the rigour of the law and all bodily sweetness; [[1:2|Smelling sweet of the best ointments|fragrantia unguentis optimis]], that is, of sublime contemplation, in which thou contemplatest the boundless worshipfulness of the divine majesty, and of excellent discretion, by which thou doest all things in order and becomingly.

paras.t: Insuper de corporalibus divinissimæ Virginis uberibus hæc queunt exponi : quæ beatissima ubera prorsus deificata sunt, ex contactu assiduo ac suctione oris adorandi incarnatique sponsi; fragrantia unguentis optimis, id est lacte virginali dulcissimo, quod Dominus universitatis sumpsit et suxit ex eis contra famem ac sitim, quas sponte ac dispensative propter nos assumpsit et toleravit. Legitur de sancto Abraham eremita et anachoreta præcipuo, quod Maria neptæ ipsius ad tempus decepta ac prostituta, ipse ut eam reduceret, militarem induit chlamydem, et tanquam alienus et sæcularis, cum ea in loco turpitudinis manducavit. Quumque illa collum ejus cœpisset stringere, et vultum deosculari, mox odorata est suavissimam fragrantiam corpusculi sancti viri, quod virtute abstinentiæ ac continentiæ suæ, etiam sensibiliter suavissime redolebat : quo facto, illa protinus est compuncta. Et tale quid de aliis quoque legitur Sanctis. Quanto magis pie credendum est, innocentissimum benedictissimæ Virginis incomparabiliter sobriæ, castæ, ac virtuosissimæ, sacrosanctum corpusculum, deificataque ubera suavissimo fragrasse odore, præsertim quum tam prædominans virtus ac puritas animæ, soleat redundare ac apparere in corpore?
paras.en: Moreover, these words can be expounded of the bodily breasts of the most divine Virgin: those most blessed breasts were wholly deified by the constant touch and sucking of the mouth of the adorable incarnate Bridegroom; [[1:2|Smelling sweet of the best ointments|fragrantia unguentis optimis]], that is, of the most sweet virginal milk which the Lord of the universe took and sucked from them against the hunger and thirst which He took upon Himself and bore of His own will and by dispensation [that is, by the ordering of His saving plan] for our sake. We read of St Abraham, a hermit and an outstanding anchorite, that when his niece Mary had for a time been led astray and become a harlot, he, in order to bring her back, put on a soldier's cloak and, like a stranger and a man of the world, ate with her in the place of shame [the margin gives: From the Lives of the Fathers]. And when she began to clasp his neck and kiss his face, she at once smelt the most sweet fragrance of the holy man's poor body, which, by the virtue of his abstinence and continence, gave off a most sweet scent even to the senses; at which she was at once pierced with compunction. And something of the kind is read of other Saints too. How much more is it to be piously believed that the most innocent and sacred little body of the most blessed Virgin, incomparably sober, chaste and virtuous, and her deified breasts, were fragrant with a most sweet odour, especially since so overmastering a virtue and purity of the soul is wont to overflow into the body and appear in it?

paras.t: Oleum effusum nomen tuum. Certum quod nomen sponsi tanto dulcius sapuit, splendidiusque effulsit in corde præclarissimæ Virginis, quo ipsum sponsum amavit ferventius, contemplabatur limpidius, ac aptior fuit ad gustandum dulcedinem sponsi istius, utpote ab omni inordinata affectione ac sensuali delectatione immunissima et intacta. Illa etenim mens apta est gustare quam dulcis sit Dominus, quæ nulla inordinata affectione inquietatur, nec ulla sensuali delectatione afficitur.
paras.en: [[1:2|Thy name is as oil poured out|Oleum effusum nomen tuum]]. It is certain that the name of the Bridegroom tasted the sweeter and shone the more brightly in the heart of the most glorious Virgin, the more fervently she loved the Bridegroom Himself, the more clearly she contemplated Him, and the fitter she was to taste the sweetness of this Bridegroom, being wholly free and untouched by any inordinate affection and sensual delight. For that mind is fit to taste that [[1 Pet 2:3|the Lord is sweet|dulcis sit Dominus]] which is disquieted by no inordinate affection and moved by no sensual delight.

paras.t: Amplius, possunt hæc verba esse sponsi ad Virginem gloriosam. Oleum effusum nomen tuum : id est, tu ipsa, o Mater carissima, visceribus internæ suavitatis tota redundans, omni misericordia affluis; tu præclarissimæ famæ es; tu portas piæ memoriæ absque insitæ tibi dulcedinis adspersione nunquam ingrederis; recordatio tui reficit mentem : ideo adolescentulæ, id est animæ innocentes ac simplices, seu recenter regeneratæ aut conversæ, et adhuc pusillæ, dilexerunt te. Te enim præ omni pura creatura amant universæ fidelium animæ, seu cuncti fideles, tanquam summam et optimam Dominam, Sanctam Sanctarum, advocatam et matrem, præcipuumque refugium et cooperatricem reparationis humanæ, cui regnum misericordiæ est commissum.
paras.en: Again, these words can be the Bridegroom's to the glorious Virgin. [[1:2|Thy name is as oil poured out|Oleum effusum nomen tuum]]: that is, thou thyself, O dearest Mother, wholly overflowing with the bowels of inward sweetness, aboundest in all mercy; thou art of most glorious fame; thou never enterest the gates of loving memory without sprinkling them with the sweetness that is inborn in thee; the remembrance of thee refreshes the mind: [[1:2|therefore young maidens|ideo adolescentulæ]], that is, innocent and simple souls, or souls newly reborn or converted and still little ones, [[1:2|have loved thee|dilexerunt te]]. For all the souls of the faithful, or all the faithful, love thee above every mere creature, as their highest and best Lady, the Holy One of holy women, their advocate and mother, their chief refuge and the fellow-worker in the restoration of mankind, to whom the kingdom of mercy has been committed.

paras.t: Trahe me post te. Quamvis excellentissima Virgo fuerit sublimiter confirmata in gratia, nihilo minus fuit viatrix, et incessanter proficere poterat ac profecit in omni virtute; et quo humilior erat, eo præcordialius omne bonum, omnem gratiam ac profectum Deo suo adscripsit, cujus pietati ac gratiæ totaliter atque humillime fuit innitens, orationibusque insistens. Ideo orans dixit : Trahe me post te, id est, tu, Deus et fili ac sponse meus, præcordia animæ meæ indesinenter allice et applica tibi, cum majori perfectione, cum calidiori affectu, cum contemplatione sublimiori. Præterea, si beatus apostolus Paulus, multique alii Sancti, in hac vita desideraverunt dissolvi, et esse cum Christo : quanto magis benedictissima ac ardentissima Virgo, præsertim post sui Filii ascensionem? Ex tunc ergo ubertim locuta est : Trahe me post te, id est, ad regnum gloriæ tuæ me transfer, et illic me tecum constitue. O quoties et quam devote ac fervide post Filii sui assumptionem ita locuta est, quando sacra loca passionis, crucifixionis, sepulturæ et ascensionis unigeniti sui Filii visitavit ! Qualiter tunc suspiravit, afficiebatur, anhelabat ad ipsum ! Qualiter sacri amoris æstuabat affectibus ! Instante vero sua assumptione, diutius separationem non ferens, affectuosissime protulit verba hæc. Ideo tunc per angelum denuntiavit ei Filius ejus, quod statim assumeretur.
paras.en: [[1:3|Draw me|Trahe me]] [[1:3|after thee|post te]] [Denis takes *post te*, "after thee", with *Draw me*; the Douay-Rheims joins it to "we will run"]. Although the most excellent Virgin was sublimely confirmed in grace, she was nevertheless a wayfarer [that is, still on the journey of this life, not yet in the glory of heaven], and could advance, and did advance, unceasingly in every virtue; and the humbler she was, the more heartfelt was her ascribing of every good, every grace and every advance to her God, on whose compassion and grace she leaned wholly and most humbly, and to whom she was instant in prayer. Therefore she said in prayer: [[1:3|Draw me|Trahe me]] [[1:3|after thee|post te]], that is, Thou, my God, my son and my bridegroom, draw the inmost heart of my soul unceasingly and join it to Thee, with greater perfection, with warmer affection, with more sublime contemplation. Moreover, if the blessed apostle Paul and many other Saints in this life desired [[Phil 1:23|to be dissolved and to be with Christ|dissolvi, et esse cum Christo]], how much more the most blessed and most ardent Virgin, especially after her Son's ascension? From then on, therefore, she said abundantly: [[1:3|Draw me|Trahe me]] [[1:3|after thee|post te]], that is, carry me over to the kingdom of Thy glory, and set me there with Thee. O how often, and how devoutly and fervently, after her Son's assumption [that is, His being taken up into heaven] did she speak thus, when she visited the holy places of the passion, crucifixion, burial and ascension of her only-begotten Son! How she sighed then, how she was moved, how she panted after Him! How she burned with the affections of holy love! And when her own assumption was at hand, no longer bearing the separation, she uttered these words with the greatest affection. Therefore her Son then announced to her by an angel that she would at once be taken up.

paras.t: Curremus in odore unguentorum tuorum. Constat Beatissimam hanc præ universis cursu profecisse celerrime, et spiritualium odore charismatum allectam, indefesse ad totius fontem beatitudinis adspirasse ac festinasse; atque ad imitandum ejus vestigia, suis orationibus, meritis et exemplis innumerabiles exaltavit electas puellas, imo utriusque sexus personas.
paras.en: [[1:3|We will run|Curremus]] [[1:3|to the odour of thy ointments|in odore unguentorum tuorum]]. It is certain that this most Blessed one advanced in her course more swiftly than all, and, drawn by the odour of spiritual gifts, aspired and hastened untiringly to the fountain of all blessedness; and by her prayers, merits and examples she has raised up countless chosen maidens, indeed persons of both sexes, to follow in her footsteps.

paras.t: Introduxit me rex in cellaria sua. Ex Scripturis elicitur, quod Paulus et Moyses Deum in hac vita per speciem clare et immediate viderunt. De Joanne quoque cantatur apostolo, Nunquam vidit tot secreta purus homo purius; sed pie censetur in hac sacratissima Virgo excepta, atque præ cunctis privilegiata : ita quod Rex ac Filius ejus, divitias gloriæ suæ ac gloriam divitiarum suarum æternalium, increatarum, clarius, jucundius ac eminentius demonstraverit suæ felicissimæ ac præclarissimæ Genitrici, quam alteri ceterorum ; sicque per contemplationem introduxerit eam in cellaria sua, in secreta et abdita sapientiæ suæ, in mansiones cœlestes, in occultissimas ac profundissimas theorias, tanquam familiarissimam secretariam et consiliariam suam, et tanquam sapientissimam sponsam ac dilectissimam suam matrem, cui utique secretiora aperuit.
paras.en: [[1:3|The king hath brought me into his storerooms|Introduxit me rex in cellaria sua]]. It is gathered from the Scriptures that Paul[[2 Cor 12:2||]][[2 Cor 12:4||]] and Moses[[Ex 33:11||]] saw God in this life by sight [*per speciem*: in His very form, not through a likeness], clearly and immediately [the margin gives II Cor. xii, 1–4 and Exod. xxxiii, 11]. Of John the apostle too it is sung: Never did a pure man see so many secrets more purely; but in this the most holy Virgin is piously held to be excepted and privileged above all: so that her King and Son showed the riches of His glory and the glory of His eternal, uncreated riches more clearly, more joyfully and more eminently to His most happy and most glorious Mother than to any other; and thus by contemplation He brought her [[1:3|into his storerooms|in cellaria sua]], into the secret and hidden places of His wisdom, into the heavenly mansions, into the most hidden and profound contemplations [*theorias*], as His most intimate secretary and counsellor, and as His most wise bride and His most beloved mother, to whom He certainly opened the more secret things.

paras.t: Exsultabimus et lætabimur in te. Hoc Virgo glorificanda in persona sua et spiritualium filiarum suarum perfectarum locuta est, quæ in sponso (sicut expositum est) gloriatæ sunt vehementer : et ipsa potissime, quæ tam pacifice, tam secretissime ac quietissime, tamque familiarissime cum ipso conversata est in terris, inspiciens et alloquens eum ad libitum, in quem sancti angeli optant prospicere ; nec poterat affectuosissima Virgo adspectibus tam gratiosissimi, speciosissimi ac delectabilissimi Pueri, ex sua mundissima carne progeniti, satiari. — Istud quoque in persona adolescentularum, id est proficientium animarum, sacratissimam Virginem alloquentium, potest exponi : quæ valde exsultant et gloriantur in ea, tanquam in pulcherrima, præstantissima, piissima, carissima et optima Domina : referendo tamen finaliter gloriationem istam ad Deum totius salutis objectum. Memores uberum tuorum super vinum. Jugiter enim reminisci debent animæ nostræ spiritualium uberum Virginis benedictæ, hoc est totius caritatis et misericordiæ ejus ad nos, quibus animas nostras tanquam benignissima mater dulciter fovet. Sed et corporalium uberum ejus debemus pure et frequenter ac delectabiliter memorari. Nonne enim suavissima sunt ubera illa ad contemplandum, quæ Regem gloriæ nutriverunt, quæ universæ fecunditatis fonti alimoniam influxerunt, quæ provisori cœli et terræ sustentaculum præbuerunt, et corpus illud dignissimum, quo sumus redempti, sic alere et ad incrementa perducere sunt electa? O ubera fecundissima ! O pulcherrimi fontes, ex quibus lactei rivi in os atque corpusculum adorandi Infantuli profluxerunt !
paras.en: [[1:3|we will be glad and rejoice in thee|Exsultabimus et lætabimur in te]]. The Virgin, who is to be glorified, spoke this in her own person and in that of her perfect spiritual daughters, who (as has been expounded) gloried greatly in the Bridegroom: and she most of all, who lived with Him on earth so peaceably, so very secretly and quietly, and so very familiarly, looking on Him and speaking to Him at will, [[1 Pet 1:12|on whom the angels desire to look|in quem sancti angeli optant prospicere]]; nor could the most affectionate Virgin have her fill of looking at so very gracious, beautiful and delightful a Child, begotten of her most pure flesh. This can also be expounded in the person of the young maidens, that is, of souls advancing, speaking to the most holy Virgin: they greatly exult and glory in her, as in their most beautiful, most excellent, most loving, dearest and best Lady, yet referring this glorying in the end to God, the object of all salvation. [[1:3|remembering thy breasts more than wine|Memores uberum tuorum super vinum]]. For our souls ought always to remember the spiritual breasts of the blessed Virgin, that is, all her charity and mercy towards us, with which she sweetly cherishes our souls as a most kind mother. But we ought also to remember her bodily breasts, purely, often and with delight. For are not those breasts most sweet to contemplate, which nourished the King of glory, which poured nourishment into the fountain of all fruitfulness, which gave sustenance to the provider of heaven and earth, and which were chosen thus to feed and bring to its growth that most worthy body by which we have been redeemed? O most fruitful breasts! O most beautiful fountains, from which streams of milk flowed into the mouth and little body of the adorable Infant!

paras.t: Recti diligunt te, o amabilissima sponsa, celeberrima Virgo, deificatissima Mater. Tota equidem bona, pia, dulcis, speciosa, amabilis es, nec quidquam severitatis invenitur in te.
paras.en: [[1:3|the rightous love thee|Recti diligunt te]], O most lovable bride, most renowned Virgin, most deified Mother. For thou art wholly good, kind, sweet, beautiful and lovable, and nothing of severity is found in thee.

paras.t: Nigra sum, sed formosa. Fuisti enim, o suavissima Virgo, nubilo dolorosissimæ compassionis, tristitiæ ac mæroris, in omni dilectissimi Filii tui passione salvifica, cooperta, impleta ac penetrata, imo doloris gladio perforata; eratque tunc in te duplicatus parturientium dolor. Et nisi te omnipotentia Filii tui conservasset, præ doloris vehementia, rupto (ut creditur) corde, mox expirasses; sed reservavit te Filius tuus Ecclesiæ suæ in magnum profectum credentium. Verumtamen in tot tribulationibus atque doloribus, in tantis angustiis ac pressuris, mansisti formosa: quia et hæc tanta compassio et afflictio tua, fuit tibi ipsi ineffabiliter meritoria, et per eam promeruisti facultatem efficaciamque præcipuam succurrendi omnibus nobis. Nempe si Paulo apostolo dicere licuit, Adimpleo ea quæ desunt passionum Christi, in carne mea, pro corpore ejus quod est Ecclesia : quanto plus sacratissimæ Matri Christi hoc dicere fas est? In hoc quoque resplenduit, o felicissima Domina, formositas tua, decor mansuetudinis tuæ, claritas patientiæ tuæ, profundissima tua humilitas, ac tuæ sanctitas caritatis, quod in tota tui unici prædilectissimi Filii amarissima et ignominiosissima passione, nullatenus mota es aliqua indignatione, aversione, impatientia adversus crudelissimos sceleratissimosque tui pretiosissimi Filii persecutores et crucifixores : a quibus et tu reputabaris vilis, iniqua, deformis, sicut tabernacula Cedar, videlicet ut impiissimi seductoris mater infelix, quum esses pulchra in anima instar pellium Salomonis, et cœliformi pulchritudine perornata, assimilata decori veri Pacifici, qui extendit cœlum sicut pellem.
paras.en: [[1:4|I am black but beautiful|Nigra sum, sed formosa]]. For thou wast, O most sweet Virgin, covered, filled and pierced through with the cloud of a most sorrowful compassion, sadness and grief in the whole saving passion of thy most beloved Son, indeed pierced through with the sword of sorrow[[Luke 2:35||]]; and the pain of women in labour was then doubled in thee. And had not the almighty power of thy Son preserved thee, thou wouldst soon have died, thy heart broken (as is believed) by the violence of thy sorrow; but thy Son kept thee for His Church, for the great advancement of believers. Yet in so many tribulations and sorrows, in such great straits and distresses, thou didst remain beautiful: for this great compassion and affliction of thine was unspeakably meritorious for thee thyself, and by it thou didst merit a special power and efficacy to succour us all. Indeed, if the apostle Paul could say, I [[Col 1:24|fill up those things that are wanting of the sufferings of Christ, in my flesh, for his body, which is the church|Adimpleo ea quæ desunt passionum Christi, in carne mea, pro corpore ejus quod est Ecclesia]], how much more is it right for the most holy Mother of Christ to say this? In this too, O most happy Lady, shone forth thy beauty, the comeliness of thy meekness, the brightness of thy patience, thy most profound humility and the holiness of thy charity: that in the whole most bitter and most shameful passion of thy only and most dearly beloved Son thou wast in no way moved by any indignation, aversion or impatience against the most cruel and most wicked persecutors and crucifiers of thy most precious Son; by whom thou too wast reckoned vile, wicked and misshapen, [[1:4|as the tents of Cedar|sicut tabernacula Cedar]], namely as the unhappy mother of a most impious seducer, when thou wast beautiful in soul like [[1:4|the curtains of Solomon|pellium Salomonis]], and adorned with a heavenly beauty, made like the comeliness of the true Peaceable One [*Pacificus*: the meaning of the name Solomon], who [[Ps 103:2|stretchest out the heaven like a pavilion|extendit cœlum sicut pellem]] [*pellis*, the word of the verse treated ("curtains"), means a skin or hide; the Douay-Rheims has "pavilion"].

paras.t: Nolite me considerare quod fusca sim, id est, considerationi angustiarum et tribulationum mearum non ita sitis intentæ, o filiæ, id est, animæ virtuosæ, ut retrahamini a mearum imitatione virtutum, formidine sustinendi afflictiones atque adversitates; quia decoloravit me sol, id est, amore Filii mei (qui est Sol justitiæ) omnia toleravi : cujus et vos debetis vestigia sequi, ac libenter ejus intuitu et amore aliquid sustinere, eique intime condolere, qui dignatus est tot ac tanta pro vestra pati salute.
paras.en: [[1:5|Do not consider me that I am brown|Nolite me considerare quod fusca sim]], that is, do not be so intent on considering my straits and tribulations, O daughters, that is, virtuous souls, as to be drawn back from imitating my virtues through fear of suffering afflictions and adversities; [[1:5|because the sun hath altered my colour|quia decoloravit me sol]], that is, I bore all things for love of my Son (who is the Sun of justice): whose footsteps you too ought to follow, gladly bearing something for His sake and for love of Him, and grieving inwardly with Him who deigned to suffer so many and so great things for your salvation.

paras.t: Filii matris meæ pugnaverunt contra me : id est, sacerdotes et Scribæ ac Pharisæi, filii Synagogæ matris meæ, me acriter persecuti sunt. Siquidem quidquid injuriæ, detractionis, amaritudinis, convitii ac tormenti meo Filio intulerunt, totum intulerunt et mihi : quæ unus spiritus eram cum Unico meo, eumque plus quam me ipsam dilexi, et magis de ejus, quam de propriis persecutionibus affligebar : quoniam innocentia, sanctitas ac dignitas ejus, mihi præ cunctis innotuit. O quam ferociter contra me pugnaverunt, quando tam dilectissimum et incomparabilem Filium, sponsum, consolatorem, mihi tam immanissime abstulerunt! Et sicut Filium meum sanctissimum, ita et me impugnaverunt convitiis et tormentis, invidiæ jaculis, oblocutionum et irrisionum aculeis.
paras.en: [[1:5|the sons of my mother have fought against me|Filii matris meæ pugnaverunt contra me]]: that is, the priests and Scribes and Pharisees, sons of the Synagogue my mother, persecuted me fiercely. For whatever injury, detraction, bitterness, abuse and torment they inflicted on my Son, they inflicted it all on me too: for I was one spirit with my Only One, and loved Him more than myself, and was more afflicted by His persecutions than by my own, since His innocence, holiness and dignity were known to me above all. O how fiercely they fought against me, when they so most savagely took from me so most beloved and incomparable a Son, bridegroom and comforter! And as they assailed my most holy Son, so they assailed me too with abuse and torments, with the darts of envy and the stings of slander and mockery.

paras.t: Posuerunt me custodem in vineis : id est, crudeles impiique Judæi Filium meum pulcherrimum, regem Messiam eis promissum, tam feraliter trucidando, meruerunt finaliter relinqui a Deo, pervenitque super eos ira Dei usque in finem, quia dixerunt : Sanguis ejus super nos et super filios nostros; itemque, Non habemus regem nisi Cæsarem. Idcirco et ego ab eis aversa, vineam Synagogæ deserui, de qua fui, et pro qua eram sollicita; et facta sum custos, advocata, mater et domina vinearum Ecclesiæ ex gentibus congregatæ.
paras.en: [[1:5|they have made me the keeper in the vineyards|Posuerunt me custodem in vineis]]: that is, the cruel and impious Jews, by so savagely slaying my most beautiful Son, the King Messias promised to them, deserved to be finally forsaken by God, and [[1 Thess 2:16|the wrath of God is come upon them to the end|pervenitque super eos ira Dei usque in finem]], because they said, [[Matt 27:25|His blood be upon us and upon our children|Sanguis ejus super nos et super filios nostros]]; and again, [[John 19:15|We have no king but Caesar|Non habemus regem nisi Cæsarem]]. Therefore I too turned away from them and left the vineyard of the Synagogue, to which I belonged and for which I had been anxious; and I was made the keeper, advocate, mother and lady of the vineyards of the Church gathered from the Gentiles.

paras.t: Indica mihi, quem diligit anima mea, ubi pascas, ubi cubes in meridie : id est, tu, præamantissime Fili, Rex gloriæ, da mihi jam interim, quamdiu in hoc sæculo nequam detineor, lucide contemplari, imo de die in diem splendidius intueri, qualiter in throno illo beatitudinis sempiternæ resideas, et in comprehensoribus lucis increatæ quiescas, eosque supersubstantiali tuæ deitatis pane reficias; atque ad gloriosam tuam præsentiam me cito digneris transferre; ne vagari incipiam post greges sodalium tuorum, id est, ne inter perfidos istos Judæos diutius perseverem, qui tuam sic persequuntur primitivam Ecclesiam ex Judaismo conversam : cujus persecutio est mihi grandis afflictio. Nempe et tu, o Fili mi, inter eos adhuc conversans, dixisti : O generatio incredula ! quamdiu inter vos ero? quamdiu patiar vos ? Qui etiam sunt greges tuorum sodalium, id est subditi pontificum, qui se jactant Dei vicarios ac ministros, quum sint pontifices synagogæ Satanæ.
paras.en: [[1:6|Shew me, O thou whom my soul loveth, where thou feedest, where thou liest in the midday|Indica mihi, quem diligit anima mea, ubi pascas, ubi cubes in meridie]]: that is, Thou, most dearly loving Son, King of glory, grant me meanwhile, as long as I am held back in this wicked world, to contemplate clearly, indeed day by day to behold more brightly, how Thou sittest on that throne of everlasting blessedness, and restest in those who possess [*comprehensores*: the blessed in heaven, who have reached the goal] the uncreated light, and refreshest them with the supersubstantial bread of Thy Godhead; and deign soon to carry me over to Thy glorious presence, [[1:6|lest I begin to wander after the flocks of thy companions|ne vagari incipiam post greges sodalium tuorum]], that is, lest I remain any longer among these faithless Jews, who so persecute Thy first Church, converted from Judaism, whose persecution is a great affliction to me. For Thou too, my Son, while still living among them, saidst: [[Mark 9:18|O incredulous generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I suffer you?|O generatio incredula ! quamdiu inter vos ero? quamdiu patiar vos]] [the margin gives Matt. xvii, 16 and Mark ix, 18; Denis's wording is closer to Mark]. And they are the [[1:6|flocks of thy companions|greges tuorum sodalium]], that is, the subjects of the high priests, who boast that they are God's vicars and ministers, though they are the priests of the synagogue of Satan.

paras.t: Sed quoniam Dominus et Salvator voluit suam benignissimam Genitricem per aliquot annos post suam ascensionem permanere in terra ad multorum ædificationem, conversionemque Judæorum, sponsus subjungit : Si ignoras, id est, quoniam utique non ignoras te, o pulchra inter mulieres, id est, omnium perfectissima feminarum, quæ non spiritum hujus mundi, sed spiritum qui ex Deo est, accepisti, ut scias quæ a Deo donata sunt tibi. Unde et in tuo cantico cecinisti : Quia respexit humilitatem ancillæ suæ, ecce enim ex hoc beatam me dicent omnes generationes : quia fecit mihi magna qui potens est, id est, Omnipotens me suam constituit matrem. Quoniam ergo id nosti et scis, te omni puræ creaturæ prælatam in dignitate; idcirco egredere et abi post vestigia gregum, id est, incredulos et aversos Judæos pie considera, et eorum pericula compatienter attende; et pasce hædos tuos juxta tabernacula pastorum, id est, carnales et vitiosos Judæos tuis refove orationibus et exemplis, ut salvos facias quosdam ex eis, quatenus per sanctorum Patriarcharum fidem et spiritualem Scripturæ intelligentiam nutriantur ac informentur.
paras.en: But since our Lord and Saviour willed that His most kind Mother should remain on earth for some years after His ascension, for the edification of many and the conversion of the Jews, the Bridegroom adds: [[1:7|If thou know not|Si ignoras]], that is, since thou surely dost not fail to know thyself, [[1:7|O fairest among women|o pulchra inter mulieres]], that is, most perfect of all women, who hast received [[1 Cor 2:12|not the spirit of this world, but the Spirit that is of God|non spiritum hujus mundi, sed spiritum qui ex Deo est]], that thou mayest know the things that are given thee by God. Hence thou didst sing in thy canticle: [[Luke 1:48|Because he hath regarded the humility of his handmaid: for behold from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed|Quia respexit humilitatem ancillæ suæ, ecce enim ex hoc beatam me dicent omnes generationes]], [[Luke 1:49|because he that is mighty hath done great things to me|quia fecit mihi magna qui potens est]], that is, the Almighty has made me His mother. Since, then, thou knowest and art aware that thou art set above every mere creature in dignity, therefore [[1:7|go forth, and follow after the steps of the flocks|egredere et abi post vestigia gregum]], that is, look with loving pity on the unbelieving Jews who have turned away, and attend with compassion to their dangers; [[1:7|and feed thy kids beside the tents of the shepherds|et pasce hædos tuos juxta tabernacula pastorum]], that is, cherish the carnal and vicious Jews with thy prayers and examples, that thou mayest save some of them, so that they may be nourished and formed by the faith of the holy Patriarchs and the spiritual understanding of Scripture.

paras.t: Equitatui meo in curribus Pharaonis assimilavi te, amica mea. Hoc, secundum expositiones præhabitas, præclarissime competit Virgini gloriosissimæ : quæ universis angelicis spiritibus facta est dignior, meritis major, mercede felicior; quæ et omnem aeriarum malitiam potestatum prorsus in se ipsa et in aliis multis auxilio suo devicit.
paras.en: [[1:8|To my company of horsemen, in Pharao's chariots, have I likened thee, O my love.|Equitatui meo in curribus Pharaonis assimilavi te, amica mea.]] According to the expositions given before, this befits the most glorious Virgin most excellently: she was made worthier than all the angelic spirits, greater in merits, happier in reward; and she utterly overcame all the malice of the powers of the air [that is, the demons], in herself and, by her help, in many others.

paras.t: Pulchræ sunt genæ tuæ sicut turturis. Virginem, præsertim adolescentulam, condecet pudor. Itaque castus pudor, verecundia sapientialis, non puerilis, erubescentia sancta, non anxia et mundana, sic abundabant in pectore Virginis summæ, quod et in roseo ejus vultu resplenduerunt, ejusque genas corporeas pulcherrime venustabant. Non procax, audax aut garrula, sed taciturna, timorata et verecunda exstitit optima Virgo, instarque turturis soli Deo in secreto intentissima fuit. Cujus collum fuit sicut monilia, id est, altitudo suæ magnanimitatis ac suæ voluntatis libertas, quæ nomine colli significantur, omni humilitate, subjectione, et obedientia ornabantur : ita quod nec magnanimitas ejus immoderate se extulit, nec humilitas ejus se inordinate depressit, nec propria libertate unquam abusa est : imo quo exstitit major, eo vere humilior fuit.
paras.en: [[1:9|Thy cheeks are beautiful as the turtledove's|Pulchræ sunt genæ tuæ sicut turturis]]. Modesty befits a virgin, especially a young one. So chaste modesty, a wise bashfulness, not a childish one, a holy blushing, not anxious and worldly, so abounded in the breast of the highest Virgin that they shone out in her rosy face too, and most beautifully graced her bodily cheeks. The best of Virgins was not forward, bold or talkative, but silent, God-fearing and modest, and like the turtledove she was wholly intent on God alone in secret. Her neck was [[1:9|as jewels|sicut monilia]], that is, the height of her magnanimity and the freedom of her will, which are signified by the name of the neck, were adorned with all humility, submission and obedience: so that neither did her magnanimity lift itself up beyond measure, nor did her humility cast itself down inordinately, nor did she ever abuse her own freedom; rather, the greater she was, the truly humbler she was.

paras.t: Murænulas aureas faciemus tibi, vermiculatas argento. Per murænulas istas intelliguntur gloriosa præconia, quibus in Scriptura commendata est excellentissima Domina : quæ præconia aurea sunt, dum de conceptione, nativitate et educatione Filii Dei ex ea laudatur. Similiter, dum beatitudo ejus et gloria commendatur, seu quando de sua patientia, humilitate, sobrietate magnificatur, præconia ejus vermiculantur argento.
paras.en: [[1:10|We will make thee chains of gold, inlaid with silver.|Murænulas aureas faciemus tibi, vermiculatas argento]] By these chains [*murænulæ*: necklaces of linked work, named from the lamprey, *muræna*] are understood the glorious praises with which the most excellent Lady is commended in Scripture: these praises are of gold when she is praised for the conception, birth and upbringing of the Son of God from her. Likewise, when her blessedness and glory are commended, or when she is extolled for her patience, humility and sobriety, her praises are inlaid with silver.

paras.t: Dum esset rex in accubitu suo, nardus meus dedit odorem suum. Per nardum, herbam spicosam, suaviter redolentem, atque naturæ calidæ exsistentem, designatur vel humillima caritas, vel ardentissima humilitas, virtuosorum actuum fructibus plena Virginis admirandæ : quæ nardus tam suavissime coram superexcellentissimo Rege fragravit, quod Regem ipsum in sinu Patris quiescentem oblectavit atque attraxit ad assumendam ex Virgine præelecta naturam humanam. Deinde Rege hoc per incarnationis mysterium in ejus utero novem mensibus commorante, aucta est fecundissimæ Virginis gratia, virtus, devotio, seque latius diffuderunt.
paras.en: [[1:11|While the king was at his repose, my spikenard sent forth the odour thereof.|Dum esset rex in accubitu suo, nardus meus dedit odorem suum]] By the spikenard, a herb that bears spikes, is sweet-smelling and of a hot nature, is signified either the most humble charity or the most ardent humility of the wonderful Virgin, full of the fruits of virtuous deeds: this spikenard gave out so very sweet a fragrance before the most surpassingly excellent King that it delighted the King Himself, resting in the bosom of the Father, and drew Him to take human nature from the chosen Virgin. Then, while this King dwelt in her womb for nine months through the mystery of the Incarnation, the grace, virtue and devotion of the most fruitful Virgin increased and spread more widely.

paras.t: Fasciculus myrrhæ, dilectus meus mihi: inter ubera mea commorabitur. Sicut Dominus Jesus Christus fuit suæ dignissimæ Genitrici materia copiosæ lætitiæ, ita et copiosæ tristitiæ. Et quidquid pro humani generis redemptione Filius ejus sustinuit, ipsa per modum fasciculi recollegit, colligavit, et cordi suo firmissime ad recolendum impressit. Et sicut quibusdam Sanctis creditur revelatum, amabilissima Virgo a Filii sui infantia gravissimos frequenter toleravit dolores, inspiciendo amantissimum suum, et manus ejus ac pedes tractando seu intuendo : quia certissime noverat et frequenter considerabat, qualiter Filius suus esset ab impiissimis crudeliter occidendus, perforandus, ac crucifigendus. Ex qua consideratione tantam interdum compassionem et afflictionem incurrit, quod venit quasi ad ecstasim et defectum : et tunc vere dicere potuit, Fasciculus myrrhæ, dilectus meus mihi.
paras.en: [[1:12|A bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me, he shall abide between my breasts.|Fasciculus myrrhæ, dilectus meus mihi: inter ubera mea commorabitur]] As the Lord Jesus Christ was to His most worthy Mother the matter of abundant joy, so was He also of abundant sorrow. And whatever her Son bore for the redemption of mankind, she gathered up like a bundle, bound it together, and pressed it most firmly upon her heart, to dwell on it. And, as is believed to have been revealed to certain Saints, from her Son's infancy the most lovable Virgin often endured the gravest sorrows as she looked on her most loving One and handled or gazed at His hands and feet: for she knew most surely, and often considered, how her Son was to be cruelly slain, pierced and crucified by most impious men. From this consideration she at times fell into such compassion and affliction that she came almost to ecstasy and fainting; and then she could truly say, [[1:12|A bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me|Fasciculus myrrhæ, dilectus meus mihi]].

paras.t: Verum ex consideratione abundantissimi fructus passionis Filii sui, et ex gloria suæ resurrectionis, ascensionis, ac plenæ victoriæ ejus, tantam consolationem concepit, quod dicere quivit : Botrus Cypri, dilectus meus mihi. Ipsa utique plenissime habuit dicere : Sicut abundat Christi passio in me, ita per Christum abundat consolatio mea; itemque, Secundum multitudinem dolorum meorum in corde meo, consolationes tuæ lætificaverunt animam meam. Ideo autem voluit Christus Matrem suam carissimam sibi in omnibus tam præcordialissime condolere, ut ipsa per hoc copiosius mereretur pro peccatoribus innumerabilibus exaudiri, et secum gloriosius coronari : quia, ut ait Apostolus, si compatimur, et conregnabimus; et, sicut socii sumus passionis, ita et consolationis.
paras.en: But from considering the most abundant fruit of her Son's passion, and from the glory of His resurrection, His ascension and His full victory, she conceived such consolation that she could say: [[1:13|A cluster of cypress my love is to me|Botrus Cypri, dilectus meus mihi]] [*Cypri*: of the cypress (or henna) shrub, or "of Cyprus"]. She above all could most fully say: [[2 Cor 1:5|as the sufferings of Christ abound in us: so also by Christ doth our comfort abound|Sicut abundat Christi passio in me, ita per Christum abundat consolatio mea]] [Denis puts the Apostle's words in the singular: "in me … my comfort"]; and again, [[Ps 93:19|According to the multitude of my sorrows in my heart, thy comforts have given joy to my soul.|Secundum multitudinem dolorum meorum in corde meo, consolationes tuæ lætificaverunt animam meam]] Now Christ willed that His dearest Mother should suffer with Him in all things so heartily, so that by this she might more abundantly deserve to be heard for countless sinners, and be crowned more gloriously with Him: for, as the Apostle says, [[Rom 8:17|if we suffer with him|si compatimur]], [[2 Tim 2:12|we shall also reign with him|et conregnabimus]]; and, [[2 Cor 1:7|as you are partakers of the sufferings, so shall you be also of the consolation|sicut socii sumus passionis, ita et consolationis]] [Denis has "as we are partakers"].

paras.t: Hinc et jam verba bona, verba consolatoria, a Filio proferuntur ad Matrem. Ecce tu pulchra es, amica mea, ecce tu pulchra: quia splendore mundissimæ virginitatis incomparabiliter radians, atque supernaturali fecunditate ac genitura divina præfulgens, corporali decore, omni exteriori moralitate, cunctorum divinorum claritate charismatum coruscans. Oculi tui columbarum, id est, columbina ac ovina simplicitate conspicui.
paras.en: Hence good words now, words of consolation, are spoken by the Son to the Mother. [[1:14|Behold thou are fair, O my love, behold thou are fair|Ecce tu pulchra es, amica mea, ecce tu pulchra]]: for thou shinest incomparably with the splendour of a most pure virginity, and art resplendent with a supernatural fruitfulness and a divine offspring, gleaming with bodily comeliness, with every outward good conduct, and with the brightness of all divine gifts. [[1:14|thy eyes are as those of doves|Oculi tui columbarum]], that is, conspicuous for a dove-like and sheep-like simplicity.

paras.t: Ecce tu pulcher es, dilecte mi, et decorus. Non enim pulchritudo immensa infinitaque sanctitas tuæ deitatis, ullam incurrit labem aut minorationem, assumendo ex me carnis substantiam, et in medio uteri mei requiescendo, atque ex me oriendo : imo per hæc tuam pietatem, dignationem, caritatem interminabilem clarius demonstrasti, et in utraque natura tu pulcher es : ut in præinductis jam expositionibus patuit. Lectulus noster floridus : id est, cellula uteri mei, in qua per incarnationis mysterium quiescere elegisti, omni flore virginitatis ac fecunditatis altissime decoratur; spiritualisque lectulus noster, videlicet pax interna, conscientia pura, contemplatio sancta, gremium caritatis, floridissimus et inviolabilis jugiter fuit. In eodem quoque materiali lectulo purissima Virgo cum dilectissimo suo sponso, infantulo Jesu Christo, creditur frequenter quievisse, cum interna jucunditate : et certe floridissimus exstitit lectulus ille, in quo duo illi vernantissimi, suavissimi, et incomparabiles flores, Virgo mater et Filius Deus, conquieverunt; ubi genitrix sanctitatis et ipsa sanctitas confluxerunt.
paras.en: [[1:15|Behold thou art fair, my beloved, and comely|Ecce tu pulcher es, dilecte mi, et decorus]]. For the immense beauty and infinite holiness of Thy Godhead incurred no stain or lessening by taking the substance of flesh from me, by resting in the midst of my womb, and by being born of me: rather, by these things Thou hast shown more clearly Thy compassion, Thy condescension, Thy boundless charity; and in both natures Thou art fair, as was made plain in the expositions already given. [[1:15|Our bed is flourishing|Lectulus noster floridus]]: that is, the little chamber of my womb, in which Thou didst choose to rest through the mystery of the Incarnation, is most highly adorned with every flower of virginity and fruitfulness; and our spiritual bed, namely inward peace, a pure conscience, holy contemplation, the bosom of charity, has been at all times most flourishing and inviolate. In that same material bed too [Denis seems to mean an actual bed, as distinct from the spiritual one], the most pure Virgin is believed often to have rested, with inward joy, with her most beloved Bridegroom, the little child Jesus Christ: and surely that bed was most flourishing in which those two most blooming, most sweet and incomparable flowers, the Virgin Mother and the Son who is God, rested together; where the mother of holiness and holiness itself came together.

paras.t: Tigna domorum nostrarum cedrina, laquearia nostra cypressina. Per domos istas, possunt intelligi corpus virgineum Matris sanctæ, et corpus salvificum Unigeniti ejus; per tigna vero cedrina et laquearia cypressina, varia horum corporum membra, instar cedri ac cypressi odorifera, et ab omni putrefactione et corruptione seu incineratione penitus aliena. Siquidem caro Christi non vidit corruptionem : nec ambigitur quin Filius ille omnipotens, naturaliter bonus et pius, amantissimam ac fidelissimam Matrem suam cum corpore et anima assumpserit in gloriam : ita tamen, quod anima ejus prius per mortem fuit a corpore separata, ac paulo post rursus ei unita. Potest quoque hic locus spiritualiter explanari, intelligendo per domos has, animam Christi, in qua plenitudo divinitatis gratiosissime ac gloriosissime, imo et per unionem hypostaticam habitavit, in qua thesauri sapientiæ ac scientiæ sunt collecti; et animam Virginis præamandæ, quæ anima cum ineffabili excellentia fuit templum Spiritus Sancti, sedes sapientiæ, domus supernorum charismatum, cella cœlicorum aromatum. Tigna domorum istarum, fuerunt virtutes perfectæ ac eminentes exsistentes in eis; earumque divinissimi actus laquearia nuncupantur.
paras.en: [[1:16|The beams of our houses are of cedar, our rafters of cypress trees.|Tigna domorum nostrarum cedrina, laquearia nostra cypressina]] By these houses can be understood the virginal body of the holy Mother and the saving body of her Only-begotten; and by the beams of cedar and rafters of cypress, the various members of these bodies, fragrant like cedar and cypress, and wholly free from all rotting and corruption, or falling to ashes. For the flesh of Christ [[Acts 13:37|saw no corruption|non vidit corruptionem]][[Acts 2:31||]]; and there is no doubt that that almighty Son, by nature good and kind, took up His most loving and most faithful Mother into glory with body and soul: yet so that her soul was first separated from her body by death, and a little after was united to it again. This place can also be explained spiritually, by understanding by these houses the soul of Christ, in which the fullness of the Godhead dwelt most graciously and most gloriously, indeed by hypostatic union, in which [[Col 2:3|the treasures of wisdom and knowledge|thesauri sapientiæ ac scientiæ]] are gathered; and the soul of the Virgin, to be loved above all, which soul was with unspeakable excellence the temple of the Holy Ghost, the seat of wisdom, the house of heavenly gifts, the storeroom of heavenly spices. The beams of these houses were the perfect and eminent virtues that were in them; and their most divine acts are called the rafters.
